title: Particle-Soliton Degeneracy in 2D Quantum Chromodynamics
abstract: Quantum chromodynamics in two spacetime dimensions admits a finite noninvertible symmetry described mathematically by a fusion category. This symmetry is spontaneously broken at long distances, leading to distinct vacua. When the theory has a mass gap, the spectrum is therefore characterized by particle excitations above a single vacuum and soliton sectors interpolating between vacua. We use anyon condensation and the representation theory of fusion categories to obtain exact results about this spectrum, exhibiting the allowed multiplets. Often, particles and solitons are in the same representation and therefore must have equal masses. Furthermore, the fusion category symmetry frequently implies the existence of certain stable states in the spectrum. The resulting degeneracies are encoded in quiver diagrams where nodes are vacua and arrows are excited states.

title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of C 14 Confronts Ab Initio Theory
abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure N = 8 , the long-lived radioactive isotope C 14 plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of C 14 has remained less precisely known than that of its stable counterpart C 12 . Here, we report a high-precision determination of the C 14 charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor of 5 and revealing a 1.9 σ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With C 12 and C 14 now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

title: Summary of the theory and modelling contributions at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025)
abstract: Abstract The contributions in magnetic fusion theory presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025) are summarized. This summary provides information on novel ideas and briefly reviews the most recent advances along the main avenues of the research, such as plasma integrated modelling, computational physics and application of artificial intelligence, fast ion instabilities, runaway electrons, disruptions, pellets, and some others. Given the current interest in bringing the magnetic fusion to the burning plasma state, the focus of the theory presentations was on burning plasma physics.

title: Summary of the contributions on magnetic fusion experiments (EX) to the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China
abstract: Abstract This paper summarizes the contributions presented in the ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’ category at the 30th IAEA fusion energy conference 2025, held in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China, from 13–18 October 2025. Conference materials are available at the FEC 2025 conference website ( www.iaea.org/events/fec2025 ), under the category ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’.

title: Radial transport of electric current by electromagnetic microturbulence in tokamaks
abstract: Abstract The turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum helps determine the rotation profiles of tokamak plasmas, and thereby their confinement and stability. The electron contribution therein has an additional consequence: even a modest electron momentum flux can correspond to a substantial turbulent flux of toroidal current, whose divergence could in principle modify the safety-factor profile. Here, using nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations, we show that electromagnetic fluctuations qualitatively alter turbulent momentum transport. In microtearing-mode-driven turbulence, the total momentum transport is inefficient relative to that of heat, yet an electron contribution associated with the turbulent Maxwell stress dominates the momentum flux. We show that this contribution exceeds an estimated scale required for turbulent current redistribution to compete with the collisional processes maintaining the bootstrap current. In the case of kinetic-ballooning-mode-driven turbulence considered, the momentum transport is found to be stronger and remains dominated by the electrostatic ion contribution; nevertheless, retaining the Maxwell stress is essential for the electron momentum flux to exceed this bootstrap-based reference scale. To enable this study, we independently implemented complete electromagnetic momentum-flux diagnostics in the gyrokinetic codes GENE and CGYRO, and verified them through linear and nonlinear cross-code benchmarks. Taken together, these results suggest that electromagnetic momentum transport may potentially be important for the coupled evolution of the rotation, current, and safety-factor profiles in high-beta tokamak plasmas.

title: Progress in reactor-core fusion technologies presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference 2025
abstract: Abstract This paper provides an overview of the recent progress in reactor-core fusion technologies within the vacuum vessel presented at the 30th International atomic energy agency fusion energy conference held in October 2025 in Chengdu, China, including plasma control, neutronics and nuclear data, tritium technologies, design and development of in-vessel components, related materials and intense neutron sources for material irradiation. Plasma control focusing on achievements for International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) and major fusion research devices are covered and the application of digital twin and Artificial Intelligence are highlighted. Research and Development results from the ITER and current devices to future demonstration fusion power plant reactors are summarized, particularly new findings, data validation, design and analysis tool improvement, properties assessment and technical solutions for critical issues.

title: Pellet induced transition from low to high confinement in separatrix phase spaces of ASDEX Upgrade
abstract: Abstract The Separatrix Operational Space (SepOS) concept [T. Eich and P. Manz Nucl. Fusion 61, 086017 (2021)] describes the operational space of tokamaks with respect to MHD, density limits and the L-H transition in terms of density and temperature at the separatrix. It has been inspired by the phase space developed by Rogers, Drake, and Zeiler [Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 4396 (1998)] (RDZ). Their idea was contested by pellet-induced L-H transitions [P. Gohil et al. Phys. Rev. Lett. 86, 644 (2001)] evaluated inside the pedestal and subsequently this theory was widely dismissed. Whether the SepOS concept face similar challenges when applied to a pellet-induced L-H transition is studied. On the low-density branch of the L-H transition, the separatrix density is temporarily increased by pellet injection, thereby lowering the L-H power threshold in agreement with the SepOS model. The results will also be discussed in RDZ's phase space. We conclude that the basic idea of the plasma edge phase space proposed by RDZ, more precisely that an increase in plasma beta at low collisionalities has a beneficial effect on confinement and at high collisionalities has a detrimental effect on confinement, was discarded unjustly.

title: Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) at the 2025 IAEA Fusion Energy Conference
abstract: Abstract The paper provides a high-level summary of the contributions given at the 30 th International Atomic Energy Agency Fusion Energy Conference (FEC2025) held in Chengdu, China, from the 13 th to the18 th of October, 2025, under the category ‘Inertial Fusion Energy’.

title: Icosahedral-group beam layouts for highly uniform direct-drive laser fusion
abstract: Abstract We investigate irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser fusion using beam layouts generated from the full rotational icosahedral group. By expanding the incident intensity in spherical harmonics, we show the selection rules imposed by exact icosahedral invariance and identify the forbidden multipole degrees. These exclusions are independent of the single-beam profile and therefore remain valid for both delta-function and finite-width beams. Using flat-top and von Mises–Fisher beam profiles, we evaluate the resulting root-mean-square nonuniformity and compare an optimized 60-beam icosahedral layout with the conventional OMEGA 60-beam geometry. For smooth beam profiles, this model predicts substantially lower nonuniformity for the optimized icosahedral layout than for the OMEGA-60 geometry, because exact low-degree cancellation is combined with efficient high-degree attenuation by the beam-profile transfer coefficients. We further examine random beam-weight imbalance and show that optimized high-beam-count icosahedral layouts remain robust over the range studied. These results establish a symmetry-based design principle for low-mode control and improved irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser implosions.

title: Axisymmetric perturbations and vertical displacement oscillatory modes driven by fast ions in tokamak plasmas
abstract: Abstract Recent progress on the theory and numerical simulations of vertical displacement oscillatory modes (VDOM) in tokamak plasmas is reported. VDOM are driven unstable by energetic particles and can have an impact on plasma disruptions, plasma edge stability and confinement. These modes are a candidate, together with Global Alfvén Eigenmodes (GAE), to explain Alfvén-frequency n = 0 modes driven by fusion alpha particles recently observed on JET (Oliver et al 2026 Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 055101). Differences in the physical mechanisms underlying VDOM and GAE are discussed. An analytic dispersion relation that contains both VDOM and ideal-MHD unstable vertical displacements (VDs) is derived. Limits on plasma elongation for stable plasma operation against ideal-MHD VDs are discussed. While VDOM are generally immune against continuum damping, if the wall is brought very close to the plasma boundary and the plasma density remains relatively large up to the last-closed-flux-surface (as in the case of H-mode discharges), the VDOM oscillation frequency may interact with the Alfvén continuum spectrum, giving rise to continuum damping. Specific types of fast ion distribution functions that can provide an instability drive for n = 0 modes are considered. Numerical simulations of n = 0 modes obtained with the NIMROD code are shown, including a preliminary assessment of the fast ion instability drive for these modes.

title: Application of low- Z materials for enhancing H-mode plasma performance and pulse duration in EAST with full metal wall
abstract: Abstract Wall conditioning plays a key role in controlling impurity accumulation and fuel recycling for achieving long pulse, high-performance plasmas in fusion device. In this work, the effects of real-time wall conditioning using low- Z materials—boron (B) and lithium (Li) powders injection—are systematically investigated and compared in the EAST tokamak equipped with a full-metal wall. Continuous boron injection effectively suppresses high- Z impurity accumulation and maintains a low effective charge ( Z eff ), reducing the core W 44+ density peak by up to ∼40%, and enabling reproducible 105 s H-mode discharges. Lithium injection also significantly improves impurity and fuel recycling control, supporting a record-breaking 1066 s H-mode plasma under lithium coating. A rigorous statistical comparison via multivariate linear regression within a shared operational window reveals that real-time lithium conditioning delivers an approximate 26% enhancement in the confinement factor H 98 compared to the real-time boron conditioning baseline, while maintaining an equivalent core Z eff . This plasma improvement is accompanied by an order-of-magnitude reduction in lower divertor neutral pressure P low,div and suppressed edge D α emissions. Analysis of the plasma profile confirms that real-time Li injection enhances wall pumping to reduce edge density, which steepens the local density gradient within the narrow pedestal region. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of low- Z material-based wall conditioning in improving plasma confinement and extending discharge duration, offering important implications for ITER and future fusion devices.

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract: Abstract Liquid metal plasma-facing components are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.

title: Tritium release and defect evolution in neutron-irradiated Li 2 Pb x Ti 1-x O 3 ceramic pebbles
abstract: Abstract Achieving tritium self-sufficiency remains a key challenge for future fusion reactors, creating a strong need for breeder materials with efficient tritium release. In this study, neutron-irradiated Li2PbxTi1-xO3 (x=0, 0.05, and 0.1) ceramic pebbles were investigated by tritium thermal desorption spectroscopy (T-TDS) and electron spin resonance (ESR). Tritium release was examined at different heating rates and under isothermal conditions, and the corresponding kinetic parameters were determined. All samples exhibited a single tritium desorption peak that shifted to higher temperatures with increasing heating rate, confirming a thermally activated release process. Pb introduction broadened the desorption peak and lowered the apparent activation energy for tritium release. Under isothermal heating, the tritium diffusion activation energy (Ed) and pre-exponential factor (D0) increased simultaneously, following the compensation effect and suggesting multiple migration pathways. ESR isochronal and isothermal annealing showed that irradiation-defect annihilation occurs in two stages: a fast stage associated with electron migration and a slower stage governed by oxygen diffusion. The defect-annihilation range overlaps strongly with the main tritium-release range, indicating that tritium release is jointly controlled by diffusion and defect evolution. Pb addition accelerates defect annihilation and broadens the defect-recovery temperature range, thereby regulating tritium migration and release through changes in defect stability.

title: Transition from Te-ITB sustainment with saturated m / n =1/1 activity to q =3/2 rational-surface-mediated collapse in EAST
abstract: Abstract A collapse of an electron internal transport barrier (Te-ITB) followed by a major disruption, is observed in electron-heating-dominant H-mode plasmas with a core- peaked Te profile on EAST tokamak. Before the collapse, the Te-ITB coexists stably with a long-lived saturated m / n = 1/1 mode, where m and n denote the poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, respectively. During this phase, the dominant electron- temperature information-transfer pathway identified by the transfer entropy (TE) analysis remains in the core region, consistent with barrier sustainment. In the pre-collapse phase, nonlinear coupling among core m/n = 1/1 modes, secondary destabilization of the saturated m / n = 1/1 mode and enhanced core impurity radiation are observed. The dominant TE response then shifts toward the q = 3/2 rational surface, while the inward-directed coupling is weakened. Although an m / n = 2/1 mode already exists before the collapse, it remains relatively passive until the heat perturbation propagates outward. The m / n = 3/2 mode emerges closest in time to the Te-ITB collapse and may participate in the final barrier degradation, which is followed by rapid outward thermal-perturbation propagation, fast-electron redistribution, enhanced impurity radiation, and finally a major disruption. These observations suggest that Te-ITB collapse is associated with the reorganization of electron-temperature information- transfer pathways and local rational-surface coupling, rather than with static magnetic- island topology alone.

title: Investigation of the Inverse Plasma Sheath via BIT1 PIC modelling
abstract: Abstract In a classical plasma sheath, the potential decreases from the upstream towards the wall. The absolute value of the potential drop depends on a number of parameters, such as the electron temperature and the flux of electrons emitted from the surface. The question then is whether the wall potential can ever exceed the plasma potential -- whether there is a realistic access to the so-called inverse sheath in tokamaks. We start our investigation from the work of Campanell and Umansky, reproduce their regime, and determine whether it is applicable to fusion-relevant conditions. Afterwards, we explore the theoretical conditions for accessing the inverse sheath.

title: Cross-machine profile prediction and differentiable optimization by learning multi-tokamak databases
abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance plasma regimes is becoming increasingly important for tokamak operation and scenario design. Conventional operation-space exploration relies on computationally expensive iterative simulations and experimental trial and error. Although machine-learning methods have recently been applied to this problem, many optimization approaches treat the predictive model as a black box. They can therefore require a large number of model evaluations and must be retrained when the objective or operational constraints change. In this work, we develop a neural-network surrogate for multi-tokamak profile prediction using public databases. Device-dependent dimensional input and output variables are transformed into appropriate normalized quantities. These normalizations of input and output variables enable the prediction model to be applied to new devices such as ITER. The surrogate forms a fully differentiable mapping from engineering parameters to plasma profiles and derived performance metrics. Automatic differentiation provides the exact Jacobian of this mapping and enables gradient-based optimization without treating the model as a black box. Under identical objectives and bounds, the proposed method requires substantially fewer model evaluations than other machine-learning approaches. The proposed framework offers an efficient route from multi-machine data to interpretable plasma optimization and reactor scenario design.

title: CarMa0NL modelling of COMPASS halo currents
abstract: Abstract A vertical displacement event in the COMPASS tokamak is modelled using the CarMa0NL code, with the halo-current width treated as a free parameter. The simulations that best reproduce the experimental evolution are those in which the resulting safety factor at the last closed flux surface remains above unity. This result is consistent with the possibility that the interaction of the \(m/n=1/1\) mode with higher harmonics, and the associated formation of a stochastic magnetic field-line structure, may contribute to setting the halo-current width. The potential relevance of this observation to scrape-off-layer widening and divertor heat-load mitigation during normal operation is discussed.

title: Effects of the momentum-dependent mean-field on collective flow in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC-STAR beam-energy scan energies
abstract: Abstract Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 3 and 4:5 GeV are simulated with the AMPT-HC transport modelto examine how momentum-dependent nuclear interactions affect hadronic observables. Comparedto the default momentum-independent potential, the momentum-dependent potential (MDI) suppressesΛ, π+, and K+ production and increases proton yields at larger absolute rapidities within0.4 < pT < 2.0 GeV/c. The directed and elliptic flows of mesons appear to be more sensitive toMDI than those of baryons. This greater sensitivity may partly arise from MDI-induced changes inparticipant-spectator momentum exchange and the associated spectator-shadowing effects. The MDIeffect on proton elliptic flow weakens systematically with increasing beam energy. These resultsindicate the importance of momentum-dependent interactions for describing collective flow at thecollision energies investigated here.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement of the S 1 0 ↔ P 3 2 Transition and a Multitransition King-Plot Consistency Test
Runaway electron induced explosions of graphite; modeling versus controlled DIII-D experiments
abstract: Abstract The state-of-the-art concerning the modeling of the thermomechanical response of graphite to runaway electron (RE) impact is based on one-way coupled linear thermoelasticity combined with Rankine’s strength-based failure criterion and limited to the onset of material failure. Here, the predictive capabilities are extended to the nonlinear damage phase characterized by material fragmentation and debris expulsion. This is achieved by introducing plasticity via the Johnson–Holmquist constitutive model, adopting an effective plastic strain-based failure criterion and coupling finite element analysis with smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. The extended thermomechanical model is successfully benchmarked against the results of two controlled RE-induced damage experiments recently carried out in DIII-D. This constitutes an important step towards the final objective of quantitatively describing the thermomechanical response of tungsten to REs.

title: Numerical investigation of helium leakage and transport from in-vessel cooling-circuit in fusion reactor using DSMC method
abstract: Abstract Early detection of micro-leaks is essential for fusion reactors because such leaks precede a large-break loss-of-coolant accident (LOCA), which can seriously threaten vacuum-vessel structural integrity and reactor safety. In high-vacuum vessels, micro-leak identification depends on the transport characteristics of the plume released from the leak, making plume simulation and feature analysis important for leak detection. However, micro-leak plumes evolve across transitional and free-molecular regimes, where conventional continuum methods become limited. The direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides a promising approach for resolving cross-regime rarefied plume transport. In this work, DSMC is used to investigate helium leak plumes in the CFEDR vacuum vessel. Representative leak locations at the inboard blanket, outboard blanket and lower divertor, together with different leak intensities, are analyzed in terms of plume morphology, pressure distribution, affected volume and probe response. The results show that the plume evolves within 1-100 ms from a directional jet into a vessel-scale diffusive field, while pressure decays by approximately two to three orders of magnitude across the chamber. The pressure responses differ among the three representative leak locations, indicating that poloidally distributed probes can provide location-dependent signal features for the future development of leak-localization methods. At a leak intensity of 5 × 10^(-5) kg/s, representative window probes reach the 10^(-4) Pa threshold within 4.35-8.50 ms, whereas lower-intensity leaks remain confined near the source and require more sensitive or cumulative detection. These findings provide preliminary guidance for multi-probe, multi-threshold monitoring strategies for early in-vessel LOCA warning in fusion reactors.

title: Neutronics characterisation of the radiation environment for the qualification of magnetic sensors on DEMO
abstract: Abstract Magnetic sensors are a primary diagnostic tool for plasma control on DEMO, required to measure the local distribution of magnetic fields at multiple positions. As these sensors must be located between the Breeding Blanket (BB) and the Vacuum Vessel (VV), they will be exposed to a harsh radiation environment, with neutron fluences expected to exceed those of ITER by up to an order of magnitude. This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of the radiation environment at the expected locations of magnetic sensors in DEMO, for both the Helium-Cooled Pebble Bed (HCPB) and Water-Cooled Lithium Lead (WCLL) BB configurations. MCNP simulations were performed using heterogeneous reference models of both blankets. Neutron and gamma fluxes, nuclear heat loads, dose rates and displacements per atom were estimated at 60 in-vessel and 60 ex-vessel positions, distributed poloidally around the plasma. The HCPB configuration produces a maximum in-vessel neutron flux of 3.6×10 13 n cm -2 s -1 at the equatorial inboard positions, a factor 18 higher than the WCLL value at the same location. The WCLL maximum in-vessel neutron flux is 8.6×10 12 n cm -2 s -1 , found below the divertor, where the shielding is less effective. The impact of the Magnetic Strip (MS) – a modular structure proposed to integrate the sensors while ensuring compatibility with Remote Maintenance (RM) – was also assessed, through a parametric study in which the radial thickness of the MS envelope was varied between 5 and 11 cm. Overall, the results presented in this paper establish the boundaries of the radiation environment that must be sustained by the magnetic diagnostic front-end components over the plant lifetime, and provide the quantitative neutronics basis for the irradiation testing and qualification program required to advance the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of the DEMO magnetic sensors from the proof-of-concept stage to full validation in a fusion-relevant environment.

title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low recycling scrape-off layer: A one dimensional gyrokinetic study
abstract: Abstract A liquid lithium boundary offers a route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length estimates presented here, can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but more complete models are needed. We present 1-D, two-velocity-space gyrokinetic simulations of low and higher-recycling LTX-beta SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line from the low-field-side midplane to the high-field-side limiter, evolving kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses with experimentally constrained mid-plane parameters. The low-recycling case develops a hotter SOL, a larger electrostatic potential variation along the field line, and a density response not recovered with an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure. This indicates that kinetic-electron dynamics and the associated ambipolar potential are important for maintaining quasi-neutrality and reducing electron end loss. Collisionality scans show that as the ion neoclassical collisionality drops below unity, the ion distribution develops a stronger non-Maxwellian structure. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, especially for low recycling, because ions become mirror trapped and electron transport is suppressed by the ambipolar potential. These results suggest that low recycling lithium walls in LTX-beta access a SOL regime where mirror trapping and electrostatic modifications alter field-line residence times relative to fluid expectations, effects expected to amplify in larger, hotter tokamaks.

title: Hybrid magnetic diagnostics on DEMO: general concept and integration studies
abstract: Abstract As tokamaks advance towards steady-state fusion operation, most plasma diagnostics will have elements exposed to increasing nuclear and thermomechanical loads over the lifetime of the facilities. Since diagnostic failure due to neutron exposure is expected to occur in such environments, the approach on DEMO has been to develop a set of diagnostics with robust front-end components compatible with remote handling. This paper outlines a general concept of a magnetic diagnostic system for long plasma-duration operation, developed for DEMO but applicable to future full-scale fusion power plants and intermediate machines like the VNS. This is achieved by employing resilient enabling technologies, hybrid magnetic diagnostic chains and data fusion estimators. Following a detailed overview of the diagnostic subsystems under development, and the characterization of the radiation environment at the most exposed front-end locations, the main interfaces with other reactor systems are described and a remote handling classification scheme is developed, based on the one adopted on ITER. An in-depth discussion of the integration possibilities for in-vessel probes and cables on DEMO is then provided. To address the constraints identified in these studies, the Magnetic Strip concept is proposed, a modular structure conceived to house all the in-vessel magnetic probes and part of the cable looms that carry the signals to the vacuum vessel feedthroughs. The Magnetic Strip is designed to be attached to the inner surface of the vacuum vessel, anchored on the fixation bosses developed for ITER diagnostics, behind the breeding blanket. Integration with the remote maintenance procedures of the blanket is demonstrated through the development of a remote handling tool concept to manipulate the structure. Preliminary analyses underline the advantages of the Magnetic Strip concept, which allows the replacement of the front-end components and cabling in single remote handling operations while keeping temperatures and thermal gradients within the operating limits.

title: The sigma meson ( f 0 ) at finite temperature with truncated overlap fermions
abstract: Abstract We study the temperature dependence of meson screening masses in two-flavour lattice QCD using dynamical truncated overlap fermions (TOFs), a type of lattice chiral fermions. The screening masses for the π , ρ , a 1 , a 0 , and the sigma ( f 0 ) mesons are extracted by computing spatial correlation functions. This exploratory study uses meson screening masses and the connected/disconnected decomposition of the scalar correlator as diagnostic observables to examine how the disconnected contribution changes across the pseudocritical region. Above the pseudocritical temperature T pc , the π and f 0 screening masses become degenerate, consistent with chiral restoration. The ( ρ , a 1 ) pair also shows the expected degeneracy. Decomposition of the f 0 propagator reveals that the connected contribution dominates above T pc , while the disconnected part becomes significant below T pc , explaining the reduced statistical clarity observed at low T . These results demonstrate that dynamical TOF simulations can capture the qualitative thermal behaviour of the scalar sector.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Quasi-doublets in the $3\alpha$ Spectrum of $^{12}$C
abstract: Abstract Within the three-$\alpha$ cluster model of $^{12}$C, we perform configuration-space Faddeev calculations of the low-lying $0^+$ and $2^+$ states. Resonance states are treated using a variant of the analytic continuation in the coupling constant (ACCC) method. The phenomenological Hamiltonian includes both two-body and three-body interactions. The recently proposed effective-field-theory-motivated leading-order (LO) $\alpha\alpha$ interaction is approximated by a Gaussian-type (LO-simulating) potential to reproduce the experimental $\alpha$--$\alpha$ scattering phase shifts.The parameters $(V,\beta)$ of the three-body force,$V_{3\mathrm{bf}}(\rho)= V \exp\!\left[-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\rho}{\beta}\right)^2\right],$are determined by fitting the experimental spectrum of $^{12}$C. We investigate the possibility of a universal set of two- and three-body interactions capable of simultaneously reproducing the energies of lowest $0^+$ or $2^+$ states. For the $2^+$ levels, we find that the condition $\beta > 3$ fm must be satisfied for such universality.The ACCC method, combined with the effective-mass approach, reveals level anticrossing and demonstrates coupling between the $0_1^+$ and $0_2^+$ states, as well as between the $2_1^+$ and $2_2^+$ states, which can be interpreted as quasidoublet structures in the $3\alpha$ spectrum.The calculated results are compared with those obtained using the Ali--Bodmer potentials and the next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) interaction. We find that the LO-simulating potential reduces the strength of the three-body force required to reproduce the low-lying spectrum.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Prospects for detecting axion-like particles via W + W − fusion at the FCC-eh
abstract: Abstract We investigate the prospective sensitivity of the FCC-eh to the axion-like particle (ALP)- W ± interaction via the ALP-mediated W + W − fusion process e − p → ν e j W + W − , followed by the semileptonic decay W + W − → l + ν l j j . Focusing on the g a W W coupling, we consider a benchmark FCC-eh configuration with E e = 140 GeV and E p = 50 TeV , assuming an integrated luminosity of 2 ab − 1 and an initial electron beam polarization of P ( e − ) = − 80 % . Under the adopted configuration, the FCC-eh can access a broad ALP mass range spanning from approximately 100 GeV to 1 TeV, with the projected sensitivity to g a W W at the O ( 1 ) TeV − 1 level. Our results indicate that the FCC-eh has considerable potential for probing the interaction between the ALP and W ± bosons.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Non-equilibrium trace of the energy-momentum tensor and bulk viscous pressure of a massive gas from kinetic theory
abstract: Abstract We investigate the far-from-equilibrium dynamics of a relativistic massive gas obeying Maxwell–Boltzmann, Bose–Einstein, and Fermi–Dirac statistics, undergoing a boost-invariant Bjorken expansion. We solve the relativistic Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation (RTA) using the method of moments. We focus specifically on the time evolution of the trace of the energy-momentum tensor Θ μ μ and the bulk viscous pressure Π , quantities that are crucial for understanding the breaking of conformal symmetry in the rapidly evolving fireball created in heavy ion collisions. Our results demonstrate that the non-equilibrium values of Θ μ μ / T 4 exhibit non-monotonic behavior, characterized by a local maximum at early times and a distinct dip around the characteristic collision time scale τ R . We find that the scaled bulk viscous pressure Π / P 0 ( P 0 isotropic pressure) depends significantly on the particle statistics. Along with this, we also observe that the magnitudes of both the bulk viscous pressure and Θ μ μ / T 4 are significantly enhanced by a larger initial chemical potential. We further find that increasing mass strongly enhances both the normalized trace and the magnitude of the bulk viscous pressure. Finally, for ensembles of randomly perturbed non-equilibrium moment initial conditions, the scaled bulk viscous pressure and pressure anisotropy lose sensitivity to the initial conditions and approach common late-time trajectories but scaled trace is not converging to a common late time trajectory.

title: Time series regression network using exogenous variables for missing effective ion charge reconstruction in EAST tokamak
abstract: Abstract The effective ion charge ( Z eff ) is a key parameter for characterizing plasma impurity levels and is important for investigating impurity transport and assessing discharge conditions in tokamaks. However, diagnostic system failures can lead to missing or incomplete Z eff signals. Accurate reconstruction remains challenging because Z eff is related to multiple plasma parameters and exhibits temporal dependencies. In this study, a time series regression network was developed to reconstruct missing Z eff values from exogenous plasma parameters in Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST). The model employed a sequential CNN-BiGRU-Transformer encoder architecture, in which the CNN extracted local temporal features, the BiGRU captured bidirectional temporal information, and the Transformer encoder modelled dependencies across different timescales through multi-head self-attention. The model was trained and validated using a dataset comprising 1566 EAST discharges. The results show that the average similarity between the reconstruction and experimental data is 90.3%, while the average coverage probability is 91.4%, indicating that most reconstruction values fall within the standard deviation error range of the experimental results. Overall, this study presents a feasible offline signal reconstruction method to maintaining the integrity of Z eff signals in EAST and provides a useful reference for reconstructing missing diagnostic data in future fusion devices.

title: Phase-space dynamics of fast ions during abrupt MHD bursts in the Large Helical Device
abstract: Abstract We investigated the phase-space dynamics of helically trapped fast ions during energetic-particle-driven magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) bursts in the Large Helical Device (LHD) using a fast-sampling fast-ion D α (F-FIDA) diagnostic based on charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. Conditional averaging synchronized with the timing of radio-frequency (RF) bursts accompanying the MHD bursts enabled the extraction of F-FIDA signals associated with the bursts. The phase-space dynamics inferred from the F-FIDA spectra showed two distinct behaviors: a rapid increase in the F-FIDA signal near the plasma edge immediately after the burst, and a delayed decrease inside the plasma occurring a few milliseconds later. The former is likely related to localized deformation and magnetic reconnection during the early phase of the MHD event, while the latter appears to be caused by rotating, downward-chirping MHD modes, leading to phase-space dynamics of fast ions. These results contribute to understanding the fast-ion transport processes during energetic-particle-induced MHD activity in fusion plasmas.

title: Performance optimisation of tokamak operation in ASDEX Upgrade through novel feedback control capabilities
abstract: Abstract Optimising the performance of tokamak operation is not only a matter of tuning individual control loops, but needs a holistic approach with a focus on the effective interplay of all control system components. The ASDEX Upgrade Discharge Control System (DCS) has enabled outstanding results of physics effect studies and operation scenario development. This is facilitated by efficient and highly robust algorithms for measurements data processing and plasma state estimation, a versatile feedback control suite, a powerful actuator management approach that optimises the utilisation of the limited number of actuators, and pulse supervision control reacting to events and plasma state conditions to achieve a maximum exploitation of the pulse and protect device and investment. Moreover, Fenix, a fast ‘flight simulator’ with a full model of the control system and a control-oriented plasma and plant model, assists in scenario design, validation and control method development, thus accelerating the turnaround time from the design of emerging capabilities to their exploitation in plasma pulses. Larger and more complex fusion devices such as ITER and DEMO in particular, will benefit from such a control structure and active contributions are being made to the architectural design of their control systems.

title: Determination of poloidal field coil currents from target plasma configuration based on deep neural network
abstract: Abstract Precise control of the poloidal magnetic configuration (PMC) is essential for optimizing plasma performance and ensuring the operational safety of tokamaks. The PMC is predominantly controlled by the poloidal magnetic field induced by a set of poloidal field (PF) coils, so determining each PF coil current ( I PF set) based on the target PMC before the experiment is crucial for achieving a desired discharge. This paper proposes a data-driven approach to determine the I PF set based on a deep neural network (DNN). Using the QUEST spherical tokamak as a case study, a dataset of PMC parameters and corresponding I PF set was generated through free-boundary equilibrium calculations. Crucially, the models are trained and validated entirely on simulated equilibria, and all predictions are benchmarked against the free-boundary equilibrium solver. Independent limiter and divertor DNN models were first trained to determine I PF set from target PMC features. These models provide approximate predictions suitable for pre-discharge feedforward design, with all coil current RMSE values below 0.56 kA. To enable unified current determination for both configuration types within a single network, an integrated model was further developed by training on the combined limiter and divertor datasets, with limiter samples embedded into the higher-dimensional divertor feature space. This integrated model achieved comparable prediction accuracy without requiring separate models for each configuration type. Additionally, the role of PF35-1 (a pair of PF coils located near the divertor target) in fine-tuning strike point positions was examined. The proposed method reduces computation time from several seconds to under 1 ms per prediction, and offers strong potential as a feedforward component within real-time plasma control systems in future tokamak experiments. The method is intended to provide approximate feedforward coil currents for pre-discharge configuration design, with centimeter-level accuracy in plasma shape, rather than high-precision equilibrium solutions.

title: Cross‐device and cross‐modal arc detection: transfer learning between EAST visible and WEST infrared diagnostics
abstract: Abstract This work presents an engineering-oriented data processing and model training pipeline for Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) visible and (W) Environment in Steady-state Tokamak (WEST) infrared data, enabling a systematic study of cross-device and cross-modal electric arc detection. A lightweight convolutional neural network is adopted as a cross-device arc detection model, and joint training and transfer learning experiments are conducted on EAST visible (VIS) and WEST infrared (IR) data. Single‐modality baselines are first trained on EAST and WEST, then evaluated zero‐shot on the opposite device, followed by a comparison of frozen‐backbone and fine‐tuned transfer for VIS → IR and IR → VIS. The results show that models trained from scratch on each diagnostic channel already achieve high precision and recall for arc detection, whereas direct zero-shot cross-modal transfer drives the arc recall on the opposite domain almost to zero. In contrast, starting from the single-modality baselines and modestly fine tuning higher convolutional layers and the classification head on the target domain can significantly restore-cross device, cross-modal detection performance, with positive class precision and recall approaching or even surpassing the single-domain baselines. Class activation map analysis further indicates that, under fine-tuned and joint training configurations, the models consistently focus on the antenna, the arc, and its surrounding scattering region, supporting physically meaningful explanations and suggesting that cross-device, cross-modal training can capture arc related structures that generalize across devices while providing a lightweight, scalable route to reusing imaging-based diagnostic knowledge with reduced annotation and retuning effort. Given that machine protection is safety-critical and that imaging diagnostics are never identical across devices, the transferability demonstrated in this work is directly relevant to equipping next-generation tokamaks such as ITER and BEST with a reliable arc-detection capability before a large native training set becomes available. On a newly commissioned device, arc events are rare, sporadic and safety-relevant, so deferring detection until a sufficiently large native training corpus has accumulated would leave the machine unprotected during the early operational phase, when limited operating experience makes the associated risks most difficult to characterize; cross-machine and cross-modal transfer instead enables a new device to inherit a usable detection capability from the outset. Accordingly, the present work is intended not merely as a benchmark of cross-domain accuracy, but as evidence that scalable, transferable arc monitoring can constitute a machine-protection layer of future fusion reactors.

title: Comparative study of nitrogen and neon seeding impacts on divertor detachment and core confinement in DIII-D high- β p plasmas with ITER-similar shape
abstract: Abstract Divertor detachment experiments with nitrogen ( N 2 ) and neon (Ne) seeding have been performed in DIII-D high- β p scenario at q 95 ∼ 6 , and the impacts of impurity seeding on divertor detachment and plasma confinement have been studied. Experimental results demonstrate that both N 2 and Ne seeding could effectively reduce the electron temperature at the divertor target ( T et ). The reduction in particle flux ( j sat ) is significantly more pronounced with N 2 seeding, indicating a superior capability of N 2 to facilitate deep particle detachment compared to Ne under these conditions. SOLPS-ITER simulations corroborate these findings, as the parallel momentum balance analysis reveals that N 2 particles are predominantly retained in the divertor region, facilitating strong radiative dissipation near the target with minimal core penetration. In contrast, Ne particles could penetrate upstream, ionize inside the separatrix and lead to higher core radiation. Consequently, the stronger power and momentum loss in the scrape-off layer (SOL) with N 2 seeding is the key to achieve lower T et and j sat compared to Ne seeding. Furthermore, statistical results suggest that the plasma confinement is maintained with both impurities, as the formation of large-radius internal transport barrier (ITB) compensates for pedestal degradation. Notably, the ITB formed with Ne seeding case is substantially stronger than that with N 2 seeding. TGYRO simulations indicate that for Ne seeding case, toroidal rotation shear and the E × B shear play minor roles in ITB formation. Instead, the dominant stabilizing mechanism is identified as the redistribution of the current density and the reduction of magnetic shear at large radius, which is strongly promoted by Ne seeding but only weakly influenced by N 2 seeding. These results provide a comprehensive perspective on the impact of N 2 and Ne seeding on detachment and plasma confinement sustainment in DIII-D high- β p operations, offering valuable insights into optimizing the core-edge integration in future fusion reactors.

title: Ground state deformation parameters of 154 Sm extracted from fusion barrier distribution
abstract: Abstract Heavy ion-induced fusion reactions, analyzed within the coupled-channels (CCs) framework, have been found to provide useful information about ground state deformation of the collision partners. We revisit the fusion reaction 16 O+ 154 Sm and examine the different coupling schemes in interpreting the measured fusion cross sections. Furthermore, we aim to extract ground state deformation parameters of the rare earth nucleus 154 Sm. Fusion barrier distribution is derived from experimental fusion cross sections using an analytic recipe, which assumes the barrier to be a multi-Gaussian function. Different sets of deformation parameters of 154 Sm, corresponding to different coupling schemes, are extracted by application of the chi-square ( χ 2 ) minimization technique. Bayesian analyses are performed for optimal estimation of uncertainties in the extracted values of quadrupole ( β 2 ), octupole ( β 3 ) and hexadecapole ( β 4 ) deformation parameters in each case. Employing the method of iNdependent Bayesian Model Averaging, β 2 , β 3 and β 4 of 154 Sm are determined to be 0.28 ± 0.06 , 0.06 ± 0.06 and 0.09 ± 0.04 , respectively. It is observed that the barrier distribution is more sensitive to minor changes in the inputs of the CCs model, in contrast to the excitation function which remains largely unaffected by such changes. The methodology used in this work has been quite effective in determining the ground state deformation parameters of 154 Sm. Similar strategy can be adopted to study the shape of other nuclei, by judicious choice of coupling schemes and careful application of the χ 2 -minimization technique.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Probing the onset of hydrodynamization in peripheral p-Pb collisions at s N N = 5.02 TeV
abstract: Abstract We estimate the multiplicity scale below which the hydrodynamic description of small systems, such as p-Pb collisions, becomes increasingly sensitive to non-hydrodynamic effects. The sensitivity of experimental observables, namely the elliptic flow coefficient, is investigated by varying the shear relaxation time within second-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics. To achieve this, a representative system of peripheral p-Pb collisions at s N N = 5.02 TeV is simulated utilizing the state-of-the-art JETSCAPE event generator. The soft-sector dynamics are modeled via a sequence of initial conditions, a pre-equilibrium stage, hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner. Transverse momentum spectra and rapidity distributions for light-flavored hadrons are extracted and compared with experimental data. The resulting increase in elliptic flow fluctuations indicates a breakdown of fluid behavior at a rapidity density of d N / d y ∼ 10 - 15 for p-Pb collisions at s N N = 5.02 TeV.

title: DeepMuon: generating cosmic-ray Muons based on optimal transport
abstract: Abstract Deep learning can learn distributions directly from data, enabling fast event simulation without hand-crafted designs or costly sampling. Yet many mainstream generators, such as diffusion models, require sophisticated architectures and multi-step denoising, which reduces throughput. Neural generators also struggle with sharp, high-kurtosis distributions common in physics, such as the cosmic-ray muon energy spectrum. Cosmic-ray muon simulation underpins non-destructive imaging, positioning and navigation, timing, and cryptography, and is traditionally performed with Monte Carlo or parametric models. Here we propose DeepMuon, a deep learning-based cosmic-ray muon generator that targets both efficiency and accuracy while addressing high-kurtosis fitting. We first apply an inverse Box--Cox transformation to reduce energy-spectrum kurtosis and simplify the learning task. We then optimize the generator with the Sliced Wasserstein Distance loss, achieving statistically consistent, one-step cosmic-ray muon generation with only a 2-layer Transformer encoder. DeepMuon also learns muon distribution patterns from limited data, enabling simulation of real detector-measured distributions. At sea level, DeepMuon substantially accelerates muon generation relative to the Cosmic-ray Shower Library (CRY). We further develop a DeepMuon-based pipeline to directly simulate underwater muon distributions and compare against CRY, demonstrating suitability for simulation and imaging tasks. For more details about our open-source project, please visit: https://github.com/wangab0/deepmuon.

title: Analysis of the elastic scattering cross-sections within the halo and non-halo configurations of 8 B and 11 Be projectiles
abstract: Abstract The optical model (OM) formalism inherently omits the structural properties of weakly bound nuclei, owing to its restriction to an effective two-body description. By assuming the halo and non-halo configurations of 8B and 11Be projectiles on two quite different mass targets, 64Zn and 208Pb, we introduce an approach that explicitly incorporates the ground-state structure of a weakly bound projectile by embedding its wave function into the projectile-target nuclear potential through a double-folding formalism. The resulting potential successfully reproduces the suppression of the Coulomb-nuclear interference peak observed in elastic scattering, which is commonly attributed to coupling with breakup channels. Moreover, incorporating the halo structure into the OM significantly improves the agreement with experimental elastic-scattering data. These results for weakly bound nuclei demonstrate that an accurate description of elastic scattering requires an OM that explicitly accounts for the projectile's structure.

title: A modular messenger benchmark for rank-two neutrino masses in lepton-number-violating R -parity violation
abstract: Abstract We study the flavor structure of Majorana neutrino masses in a modular messenger realization of lepton-number-violating R -parity violation. Homogeneous level-three modular symmetry, with Γ 3 ′ ≃ T ′ and an even-weight sector descending to A 4 , relates bilinear and third-family lepton–quark couplings at a common modulus. Renormalizable mediator chains generate these interactions, and baryon triality forbids the baryon-number-violating operator. The charged-lepton and soft-sector alignments define the benchmark. The retained neutrino mass texture contains neutralino-tree and bottom–sbottom rank-one contributions and leaves one neutrino massless. For a weight-four loop direction, a bilinear displacement within the weight-two and weight-four plane preserves the massless mixing column. A symmetric weight-six loop contribution allows both deformations to change that column. The extended textures accommodate both neutrino mass orderings. Four 501 × 501 modulus profiles determine their oscillation-compatible regions and associated mass and flavor observables. Representative solutions give m β β between 1.47 and 3.75 meV for normal ordering and between 17.8 and 48.2 meV for inverted ordering, within the kinematic envelope of a massless neutrino spectrum. The mass sum and beta-decay mass-parameter provide complementary ordering signatures. We connect the fitted flavor coefficients to weak-scale neutralino and sbottom contributions by inverse matching and derive a conditional charged-current neutralino-decay flavor correlation.

Production of vacuum particles from relativistic scalar particles in a deformed spacetime
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the quantum dynamics of relativistic scalar particles in a (1+1)-dimensional de Sitter spacetime deformed by rainbow gravity, in which the spacetime metricdepends explicitly on the energy of the probing particles. We begin by deriving the covariantKlein–Gordon equation in this modified gravitational background and obtain its exact solutionsby two independent methods, in terms of Whittaker and Hankel functions. Building upon thisformulation, we analyze the corresponding energy spectrum and the semiclassical solutions, andsubsequently examine vacuum particle production within the Bogoliubov approach. Both sets ofsolutions lead to the same particle number density, which takes the form of a thermal Bose–Einsteindistribution depending only on the temporal rainbow function f_1. In the large-mass limit, it reducesto a Boltzmann factor characterized by an effective Gibbons–Hawking temperature T = f_1H/2π,showing that rainbow gravity rescales the de Sitter horizon temperature and can either enhance orsuppress particle creation relative to general relativity.

title: Form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD tomography of N → ∆(1232) multipole structure
abstract: Abstract A form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD reconstruction is developed for the \(N\to\Delta(1232)\) electromagnetic transition. The production input consists of the published CLAS magnetic multipole amplitude and electric and scalar/Coulomb quadrupole ratios. Additional external low-\(Q^2\) ratio data are retained only as a separate ratio-sector diagnostic. The electroproduction quantities are propagated replica by replica and converted to the dimensionless Jones--Scadron transition form factors \(G_M^*\), \(G_E^*\), and \(G_C^*\). AICc model selection yields a modified dipole for \(G_M^*\), a dipole for \(G_E^*\), and a cubic \(z\) expansion for \(G_C^*\). These fits define the imposed positive-\(x\) normalization \(F_\alpha(t)=2G_\alpha^*(-t)\) for factorized, correlated exponential, Regge-like, and double-distribution-inspired transition-GPD profiles. The upper boundary of the impact-parameter transform is fixed by the largest measured absolute-form-factor point, \(Q^2=6~\mathrm{GeV}^2\), so that no high-\(Q^2\) continuation beyond the measured range enters the production reconstruction. The primary transverse localization observable is therefore defined from the small-\(Q^2\) slope of the modeled transition GPD, with finite-window radial moments retained only as secondary core-shape diagnostics. \textcolor{red}{For the slope-defined width, the transition form factor contributes an \(x\)-independent channel-dependent offset, while the entire \(x\) dependence is fixed by the chosen longitudinal--transverse profile ansatz. The factorized profile is \(x\)-independent and the three non-factorized families generate distinct modeled \(x\) dependences.} The resulting reconstruction separates measured transition-form-factor information from model-dependent longitudinal structure and provides a controlled framework for assessing structural and covariance sensitivity in \(N\to\Delta(1232)\) transition tomography.

title: Competing valence and core-excited configurations in the level structure of doubly odd neutron-deficient \textsuperscript{60}Cu : shell-model perspective
abstract: Abstract To reveal deeper insights into the pattern of nucleon excitations within the \textit{fp} shell along with the possibility of excitation to the deformation-driving 0\textit{g$_{9/2}$} orbital in the neutron-deficient and nearly magic $^{60}_{29}$Cu$_{31}$ nucleus, comprehensive shell-model calculations have been carried out using two different model spaces, viz. \textit{f$_{5/2}$pg$_{9/2}$} and full \textit{fp}. The predicted values of level energies and branching ratios are compared with the available experimental data. The electric quadrupole moments as well as the reduced \textit{E}2- and \textit{M}1-transition strengths are calculated to probe the possibility of the onset of deformation and collectivity. The particle configurations involving only the upper \textit{fp} shell are found to play the dominant role in generating the low-spin ($J$ $<9\hbar$) positive-parity states, whereas the breaking of the $^{56}$Ni core and the neutron excitations from the \textit{fp} shell to the 0\textit{g$_{9/2}$} orbital provide significant contributions in constructing the wave functions of the positive-parity states lying above the 8$_{1}^{+}$ state. All negative-parity states involve contributions from the 0\textit{g$_{9/2}$} orbital. The plausible presence of prolate and/or oblate deformed states as well as the octupole-correlated states is discussed. The underlying features of the isobaric analogue states in the $^{60}$Cu--$^{60}$Ga isobaric pair are also presented by utilizing an appropriate set of residual interactions.

title: Clock-WEP tests of string-derived dilaton and modulus sectors
abstract: Abstract String compactifications and runaway-dilaton models can contain light scalar directions. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. Its gauge kinetic functions, matter-metric or Yukawa slopes, source charge, scalar trajectory, and scalar range determine a Damour--Donoghue WEP vector and a clock-drift vector. The analysis uses this map to compare such sectors with weak-equivalence-principle (WEP) and clock data. The numerical fit assumes one effective long-range scalar, or an aligned direction in a multi-field space. With that assumption, WEP tests and secular clock drifts probe related projections of the same scalar-slope vector. The minimal two-charge Damour--Donoghue fit uses Ti--Pt MICROSCOPE, Be--Ti torsion-balance, and $^{85}$Rb--$^{87}$Rb atom-interferometer data, then adds the Yb$^+$ E3/E2 secular $\alpha$-drift row. The WEP-only fit gives $D_{\hat m}=(-6.06\pm34.91)\times10^{-12}$ and $D_e=(8.80\pm46.46)\times10^{-12}$, with correlation $-0.99958$. The clock input is $\dot\alpha/\alpha=1.0(1.1)\times10^{-18}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. It matches the WEP marginal reach when $|\zeta|=2.37\times10^{-8}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, with $\zeta=\dot\varphi/\alpha_E$. For the benchmark $\dot\varphi=\xi H_0$ and $\alpha_E=10^{-3}\alpha_0$, this gives $\xi/\alpha_0\simeq0.34$. This value marks equal information between the clock row and the WEP marginal constraint. A model becomes testable after it supplies $r=D_{\hat m}/D_e$, the scalar amplitude, and $\zeta$. As an example, the Damour--Piazza--Veneziano runaway-dilaton estimate lies near $\eta\sim10^{-12}$ for order-unity $n=2$ parameters, well above the MICROSCOPE-level WEP scale. In the representative-isotope two-charge model, a MICROSCOPE-level Be--Ti-like row would reduce the long WEP axis by a factor $27.8$; a repeated Ti--Pt-like row would barely change it. The calculation tests compactification-level predictions for string-derived dilaton or modulus sectors after the model supplies its low-energy data.
