title: Dihadron Transverse-Spin Asymmetries in Muon-Deuteron Deep-Inelastic Scattering
abstract: In 2022, the COMPASS collaboration performed semi-inclusive measurements of deep-inelastic muon-scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron ( LiD 6 ) target. From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries are directly sensitive to the quark transversity distributions and provide an independent handle on these fundamental quantities with respect to the Collins asymmetries measured in single-hadron production. The present results significantly improve upon the previous COMPASS deuteron measurements, which were the only available deuteron data worldwide, and reach a statistical precision comparable to that of the existing proton results from COMPASS. A small but nonzero asymmetry is observed at large Bjorken- x , consistent with theoretical expectations. A point-by-point extraction of the valence-quark transversity distributions yields, in particular, a substantially improved determination of the d -quark transversity. These measurements represent a major step towards a complete flavor mapping of the transverse-spin structure of the nucleon.

title: Two-dimensional transport mechanisms in the vicinity of the X-points in snowflake divertors
abstract: Abstract Snowflake divertor (SFD) experiments show enhanced radial transport near the X-points, more than may be explained by standard two-dimensional edge transport models without drifts. Here we investigate transport mechanisms in SFDs through two complementary approaches: i) modelling of recent SFD experiments performed at MAST-U with the edge transport code UEDGE with ExB and ∇B drifts enabled, and ii) reduced modelling of transport and turbulence in the vicinity of the X-points with a model developed here and implemented in BOUT++. Through these two approaches we assess the two leading candidates for this transport: equilibrium ExB drifts driven by strong poloidal gradients near the primary X-point, and the 'churning mode' (CM), a toroidally-symmetric plasma vortex close to the X-points. UEDGE modelling shows that equilibrium ExB drifts do play a role in increasing particle and energy transport across the primary separatrix, increasing the proportion of heat flux delivered to secondary strike points (SPs) and reducing peak heat fluxes at the primary SPs. This mechanism is less effective in the upper divertor due the reversed drift directions in combination with the device geometry. Including drifts in the model is also shown to improve agreement with the experimental radiated power profiles.To self-consistently compare the impact of drifts and the CM we develop a reduced-MHD model which includes both effects, and which is implemented in BOUT++. We find that equilibrium ExB drifts are dominant when the ratio of plasma pressure in the null region to poloidal magnetic pressure at the midplane is low, β pm ≤ 0.5-1.0%, which were the conditions obtained in the MAST-U experiments. The CM was found to be dominant for β pm ≥ 1.0%, leading to increased transport across the null region and activation of secondary divertor legs.

title: Three-dimensional assessment of toroidal heat-load distribution on divertor targets in EAST
abstract: Abstract Although actively cooled W/Cu monoblock targets are designed for high steady-state heat exhaust, local overheating and damage have been observed on these targets in EAST. These observations indicate that, beyond the nominal heat-removal capability, the practical thermal margin can be affected by engineering alignment, target geometry and plasma operating conditions, which modify the local surface-normal heat flux through magnetic incidence and magnetic shadowing. In this work, the toroidal heat-load distribution on EAST divertor targets is analysed by combining infrared thermography, finite-element heat-flux inversion and three-dimensional field-line tracing using PFCFlux. The analysis focuses on the effects of toroidal-field ripple, ripple-coupled cassette misalignment and divertor target geometry. The 16-fold toroidal-field ripple produces a 2π/16 modulation of the peak heat flux on the present upper outer target, with a peak fluctuation amplitude of approximately 17.75%. Under a peak heat-flux constraint of Qsafe = 10 MW m-2, the allowable average heat flux decreases from 4.28 MW m-2 without ripple to 3.94 MW m-2 with ripple. When ripple and relative cassette misalignment are considered together, it is further reduced to 3.11, 2.79 and 2.27 MW m-2 for Delta = 0.6, 1.0 and 3.0 mm, respectively. Comparison with the lower divertor shows that improved toroidal continuity reduces ripple-only peak amplification. Using the lower outer horizontal target as a reference, the new upper horizontal target reaches an allowable average heat flux of 4.70 MW m-2 under ripple and Δ = 1 mm misalignment. These results show that magnetic ripple, assembly tolerance and toroidal geometric continuity should be considered together in divertor thermal design.

title: The influence of ELM-like loading on tungsten under slow transient conditions in Magnum-PSI
abstract: Abstract ITER is anticipated to operate with occasional slow transients, resulting in an increase in expected heat loads to the divertor from 10 to 20 MW m − 2 and thus in the surface temperature increasing to > 2000 ∘ C. At the same time mitigated ELMs may be expected to strike the surface. To investigate the consequences of this, two sets of experiments were carried out in Magnum-PSI, representing the first experiments to explore this regime. In the first set, seven ITER-like tungsten monoblocks were exposed to either hydrogen plasma, or impurity-seeded hydrogen plasma at a surface temperature of 2050 ∘ C. Simultaneously five of the seven monoblocks were exposed to 10 5 ELM-like pulses using a 1 ms duration laser at an energy density of 0.1 − 0.19 MJ m − 2 . Very strongly roughened and cracked laser exposed areas with localized melted regions were observed. These areas protruded several hundreds of micrometers above the original surface. In the second experiment, three tungsten plates, with either small, large or no castellations cut into the surface, were exposed to a hydrogen plasma at 2100 ∘ C with a wider range of ELM-like pulse numbers ( 10 2 − 10 5 ) and energies ( 0.13 − 0.31 MJ m − 2 ). The surface was found to evolve by roughening and pre-crack formation towards similar strongly protruding roughened structures as pulse number increased, while increasing the transient energy resulted in increasing the fraction of surface melting observed in the loaded region. Mass loss measurements of the plates indicated that erosion was significant, between 0.05–0.13 nm per pulse for the different plates. Extrapolating these results to ITER suggests that this mass loss rate would be relatively high and would constitute a significant tungsten source.

title: The bootstrap current in the standard and strongly inward-shifted LHD configurations in the 1/ν and plateau regimes
abstract: Abstract While a tokamak has a plasma current disruption, a helical system is much robust because the current-less operation is, in principle, possible. However, a bootstrap (BS) current due to the pressure gradient could be concerns because it could change the rotational transform. We conducted experiments on the BS current in the Large Helical Device (LHD) in the 1/ν and plateau regimes using three magnetic axis configurations Rax = 3.75 m, 3.6 m and 3.53 m with completely balanced neutral beam injection (NBI). As a reference, we use the standard configuration of Rax = 3.75 m. We then examine the inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.6 m, and the strongly inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.53 m, which is referred to the neoclassically optimized configuration [1, 2]. It was demonstrated that a clear reduction of the BS current is observed for Rax = 3.53 m than that for Rax = 3.75 m, together with a confinement improvement. Based on these experimental results, the BS current coefficient has been derived, which helps to predict the BS current in a helical fusion reactors.

title: The FAST tool for synthetic SXR calculations and determination of impurity density and effective charge ( Z eff )
abstract: Abstract A new soft x-ray (SXR) synthetic tool has been developed: it is called FAST for FLYCHK-based Atomic physics and SXR Tomography. It is based on FLYCHK SXR emissivity spectra calculated for a variety of elements, from deuterium to tungsten. FAST creates 2D plasma emissivity for arbitrary plasma compositions and plasma profiles. It computes line-integrated SXR profiles based on a specific detector geometry and response. This tool is used to reproduce signals from an absolutely calibrated multi-energy SXR (ME-SXR) camera at WEST. Thanks to its energy-resolved measurement capability, the ME-SXR camera is able to separate spectral regions dominated by impurity line emission from others containing only continuum emission. At WEST, FAST and the ME-SXR camera are employed to determine impurity density profiles for tungsten and nitrogen (used as a proxy for low- Z impurities), as well as the plasma effective charge ( Z eff ), through SXR measurement reproduction at different energies, from 2 to 14 keV. Tungsten density is determined in two plasma scenarios at WEST: lower hybrid heating in the X -point radiator regime and lower hybrid heating with modulations of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH). In the first scenario the tungsten profile is found to be moderately peaked in the core with a concentration of 0.8–1 × 10 −4 . This concentration is found to increase up to 1.4 × 10 −4 during ICRH. Tungsten peaking factor in steady-state conditions is also retrieved and compared to theoretical predictions. It is found to be slightly lower than the combined neoclassical and turbulent transport prediction.

title: Revisiting p 11 B fusion: Updated cross-sections, reactivity, and energy balance
abstract: Abstract Recent experimental progress has substantially improved the available cross-section data for the p-$^{11}$B fusion reaction, particularly in energy regions that previously lacked direct measurements. In this study, we develop a high-precision analytical parameterization of the p-$^{11}$B reaction cross-section over the 0--10 MeV energy range, incorporating the new experimental data into a continuous and numerically efficient representation. Using this parameterization, we evaluate the thermonuclear reactivity of the p-$^{11}$B reaction and examine the effects of the dominant resonance at 0.6 MeV and a newly observed resonance around 4.7 MeV. Furthermore, we assess the energy balance by analyzing the fusion power density and the electron bremsstrahlung power density. Our results indicate that p-$^{11}$B fusion is not precluded by bremsstrahlung constraints when contemporary cross-section data and self-consistent thermal modeling are employed.

title: Real-time CXRS analysis on HL-3 tokamak with reliable neural networks and cross-device transfer learning
abstract: Abstract We present a neural network-based method for real-time charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) analysis on the HL-3 tokamak. To enhance model performance and reliability, we tailor the network architecture to the physical characteristics of CXRS spectra: the receptive field matches the Doppler-broadened line width, channel embedding encodes spatial awareness across diagnostic channels, and attention pooling focuses on the most informative spectral regions. These designs yield millisecond-level inference (0.56 ms per 32-channel) with accuracy comparable to conventional methods ( R 2 _ T i = 0.93, R 2 _ v t = 0.98). Furthermore, the model’s reliability is established through interpretability and uncertainty analysis. Interpretability analysis confirms that the model focuses on the Doppler-broadened wings of C VI for T i and tracks line shifts for v t , consistent with physical principles. Uncertainty estimates show that the model appropriately expresses higher uncertainty in regions where predictions are inherently more challenging. To address data scarcity on new devices, transfer learning from HL-2A tokamak markedly boosts performance in low-data regimes while retaining a modest advantage even with full HL-3 data, provided that the spectra are properly aligned and baseline subtracted. This work establishes a real-time, reliable, and data-efficient AI framework for CXRS analysis, offering a practical path to deploy machine learning approaches in plasma control on future fusion devices.

title: Optimization of room-temperature targets for laser direct-drive fusion
abstract: Abstract Fusion ignition is a critical milestone toward the realization of fusion energy. For laser direct-drive fusion, the cryogenic deuterium–tritium (DT) targets encounter considerable fabrication and delivery challenges, such as the survival of cryogenic targets during the injection and flight in a reactor chamber. To mitigate the cryogenic bottlenecks, we explore the potential of room-temperature solid targets composed of low- Z elements and hydrogen isotopes via machine-learning optimization. In this work, a multi-fuel module is developed with the one-dimensional hydrodynamics code (MULTI-IFE) to simulate multiple room-temperature fuels. By optimizing the target structure and laser waveform parameters, a calculated fusion energy gain of 10.18 can be achieved with 2.35 MJ of laser energy, despite the additional radiative and conductive losses that may arise from the low- Z ions in the room-temperature target. A thicker target driven by a laser energy of 9.4 MJ is able to produce 109.7 MJ fusion energy with a maximum in-flight-aspect-ratio smaller than 17. During the fusion burning, tritium breeding via neutron–lithium reactions increases the fusion energy output for the LiBD 2 T 2 target by 5.2%. This work provides a reference for the ongoing development of direct-drive repetition-rate laser fusion energy.

title: Off-normal simulations of radiative collapse events in Alcator C-Mod
abstract: Abstract In preparation for ARC, supplementary offline tools are being developed alongside a real-time warning system in order to reduce its disruptivity. This paper introduces Off-Normal SIMulations (ONSIMs) to the MOSAIC pulse-simulating framework with that intent in mind. These modules probe simulated equilibria with a library of distinct perturbations, and can characterize disruptivity based on the scenario’s resiliency to them. This paper addresses the development of a module for simulating radiative collapses, with a specific focus on validating for the first time the power balance dynamics characteristic of these events. The simulations are performed using the TORAX transport simulator and are benchmarked against radiative collapse precursors on Alcator C-Mod. It is found that transport models that include sufficient turbulence effects, like a surrogate of the QuaLiKiz (Bourdelle et al 2015 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 58 014036; Citrin et al 2017 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 59 124005) transport model, are capable of reproducing the relevant radiative collapse dynamics for an L-mode discharge. It is also found that these dynamics are relatively insensitive to the shape of the collapse-inciting impurity profile, which bodes well for the robustness when probing various equilibria. The benchmarking reported here is part of a larger ongoing validation effort, which lays the groundwork for radiative collapse ONSIMs. Future work will be done to translate validations like this to a general implementation of ONSIMs to SPARC and ARC scenarios.

title: Nanosecond-LIBS-induced deuterium outgassing, diffusion, and surface modification in tungsten coatings
abstract: Abstract Tritium retention in plasma-facing components(PFCs) must be strictly controlled to ensure the safe operation of fusion devices. In ITER, compliance with the tritium inventory limit and assessment of fuel-removal strategies require in situ monitoring of fuel retention in PFCs. Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy(LIBS) is a diagnostic technique that can be implemented via remote handling to investigate fuel retention during maintenance shutdowns at ITER.In LIBS diagnostics, the selection of laser parameters plays a critical role in determining the ablation characteristics and thermal perturbation of the target. Used nanosecond(ns) laser pulses deliver energy on timescales that allow substantial thermal diffusion into the target, which could result in surface heating and melting. Under multi-pulse LIBS operation, these cumulative thermal effects can alter deuterium quantification, as deuterium may diffuse or outgas due to heating induced by earlier pulses. Such laser-induced perturbations can compromise accuracy of quantitative deuterium measurements if they are not properly accounted for in modelling.In this study, subsequent in situ ns-LIBS and in situ Nuclear Reaction Analysis(NRA) measurements were performed in Magnum-PSI on compact and porous tungsten coatings using a defocused, millimetre-scale laser spot(2.5×2.5mm). Deuterium retention and depth profiles were determined in and outside the LIBS crater. Under the investigated laser conditions, NRA measurements indicated a 66–79% reduction in retained deuterium within the sampled region of the LIBS crater, whereas pure material removal by ablation would account for only 21–42%, demonstrating additional laser-induced outgassing. Compact coatings further exhibited melting and intermixing with the underlying substrate. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for defocused ns-LIBS-induced perturbations in retention measurements. Further experimental and modelling studies are needed to assess the dependence of these effects on laser spot geometry and to determine whether picosecond(ps) LIBS, together with consideration of cumulative multi-pulse effects, could improve the reliability of fuel-retention diagnostics in future fusion devices.

title: First observation of anisotropic distribution evolution of hydrogen fast ions heated by ICRF in EAST
abstract: Abstract The continuous energy and pitch-angle distribution of hydrogen fast ions generated by ion cyclotron range of frequencies (ICRF) minority heating is measured in EAST using an imaging neutral particle analyzer (INPA). The measured two-dimensional fast-ion distribution exhibits a triangular structure: as energy increases, the pitch-angle distribution becomes progressively narrower, with its peak located around 0.4 < | v ∥ / v | < 0.5 . This behavior is consistent with resonance localization theory, which associates the pitch-angle peak with trapped orbits whose turning points are close to the ion cyclotron resonance layer. Through diagnostic response correction, the reconstructed spectrum shows a progressive enhancement of the high-energy minority-ion tail with rising ICRF power. A clear anisotropic evolution of the fast-ion distribution is also observed between discharges with different electron-temperature profiles. In the discharge with higher core electron temperature, the signal enhancement appears mainly for fast ions at energies above 100 keV and | v ∥ / v | ⩾ 0.5 , together with a broader measured pitch-angle distribution. This behavior is interpreted as the combined result of collisional pitch-angle scattering, fast-ion accumulation, and finite-orbit-width effects. The enhanced signal region corresponds to wide-orbit fast ions whose inner orbit legs extend to the hotter inner plasma region, making them more sensitive to changes in the electron-temperature profile. These results demonstrate the capability of INPA to resolve the anisotropic evolution of ICRF-heated fast ions and provide experimental insight into the optimization of ICRF heating schemes in EAST and future fusion devices.

title: Estimating global energy fluxes during COMPASS disruptions via magnetic measurements
abstract: Abstract During tokamak disruptions, a significant amount of poloidal magnetic energy is converted into other energy forms within the plasma, contributing to the thermal load on the first wall and the surrounding plasma facing components. The amount of magnetic energy converted to plasma thermal losses depends on the duration of the current quench as compared to the electromagnetic time of surrounding conductors. We implement a first-principle method to estimate plasma thermal losses during disruptions for the tokamak COMPASS. The method assumes the plasma evolves through MHD equilibrium states during the disruption, but it does not require any equilibrium reconstruction, elaborating exclusively raw magnetic measurements. The robustness of the method is validated against numerical simulations and different diagnostic measurements. An extensive analysis of energy fluxes during COMPASS disruptions is considered, showing how the poloidal magnetic energy influx contributes to losses and the role of halo currents in the task.

title: Effects of uniaxial strain and free hydrogen/helium atoms on helium bubble coalescence in tungsten divertor
abstract: Abstract Tungsten (W) is a preferred plasma-facing material for fusion reactor divertors. During service, high heat loads induce considerable thermal strain, while large amounts of free hydrogen (H) and helium (He) atoms accumulate in the W matrix. These factors promote the nucleation and coalescence of near-surface He bubbles, affecting the service safety of plasma-facing components and the transport behavior of hydrogen isotopes. However, the combined effects of strain and free H/He atoms on He bubble coalescence in W remain unclear. This work employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to systematically investigate the mechanisms by which uniaxial strain and free H/He atoms affect He bubble coalescence in W. The analysis is further combined with the thermal strain characteristics of divertor service conditions and the equilibrium pressure behavior of He bubbles. The results show that both tensile and compressive strains promote He bubble coalescence, while compressive strain has a stronger effect. Tensile strain facilitates bubble expansion by reducing the local atomic density, whereas compressive strain increases the internal He bubble pressure and accelerates He bubble connection. In H-containing systems, H concentration shows a dual effect: low H concentration promotes coalescence, whereas high H concentration suppresses it due to competition for defect sites around He bubbles. In H–He coexisting systems, free He atoms form He or H–He clusters, which redistribute H atoms and reduce H adsorption by pre-existing He bubbles. A modified equilibrium-pressure relation was further introduced to describe strain-assisted He bubble coalescence. These results provide atomic-scale insight into He bubble evolution in divertor W under complex service conditions.

title: Effects of tungsten radiative cooling on impurity, heat and momentum transport in DIII-D plasmas
abstract: Abstract A first-of-its-kind experiment was conducted in the DIII-D tokamak under WEST similarity constraints on plasma shape and core parameters. This work presents a detailed transport study comparing a reference regime dominated by intrinsic carbon radiation and a high-radiation regime resulting from controlled tungsten (W) injection using the laser blow-off system, with a core tungsten concentration n W / n e ∼ 3 × 10 − 4 and a radiated-power fraction f rad > 0.5 . The W-induced radiative cooling lowered the electron temperature, thereby decreasing T e / T i and stabilizing trapped-electron-mode (TEM) turbulence. This transition in turbulence regime reduced momentum and ion thermal diffusivities, yielding ion temperature peaking and a factor-of-two increase in toroidal rotation. At the outer plasma region, enhanced E × B shear and increased collisionality further suppressed ion-scale turbulence, causing a sharp drop in ion heat flux. Consequently, impurity transport, predominantly turbulent in the low-radiation regime, acquired a strong neoclassical inward W convection during radiative cooling, bootstrapping the cooling cycle. Despite f rad > 0.5 , radiative collapse was not observed, likely owing to collisional ion-to-electron energy exchange acting as an electron-energy reservoir, together with 1 / 1 MHD activity modulating the radiated power through core impurity neoclassical T i -screening. These results support preparation for a tungsten wall change in DIII-D by elucidating tungsten-induced turbulence stabilization. They also provide key insights for interpreting plasma performance in WEST and are relevant to future reactors expected to operate with radiating tungsten-walled plasmas.

title: Core-edge integrated modeling of ARC: on the effect of impurity transport and detachment conditions
abstract: Abstract Integrated modeling of the flat-top phase of ARC H-modes has been conducted to assess the feasibility of high-performance scenarios compatible with divertor detachment. The analysis incorporates self-consistent evolution of impurity radiation and density profiles, demonstrating that fusion power levels approaching a GW can be achieved while maintaining divertor temperatures below 2 eV with Ar seeding. Sensitivity studies reveal a strong dependence of fusion power on the separatrix density, with performance spanning 750–1000 MW, and a weaker dependence on enrichment factor and pedestal density. Alternative seeding strategies using Neon have also been explored. Plasmas with Argon seeding consistently access H-mode, providing the highest fusion power and detached divertor operation, whereas Neon seeding leads to lower performance (600–850 MW) and less robust H-mode access, due to excessive core impurity accumulation. A small W impurity peaking has been found, with decreasing values at higher Z eff . Further analyses incorporate reduced momentum transport modeling, and sensitivity studies of neoclassical impurity transport, confirming the robustness of the results. Overall, these findings support the viability of high-performing H-mode operation in ARC, ensuring divertor protection, enabled through Argon and Neon impurity seeding.

title: Quasilinear Theory of Fast Flavor Instabilities
abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasilinear theory, including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino-flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave-wave processes. In a statistically homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. Our results provide the first theoretical interpretation for the numerical observations. They also show that flavomon phases have little influence on the final state, supporting the quasilinear theory as a framework for capturing flavor evolution without resolving nonlinear small-scale dynamics.

title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order QCD Corrections to Photon-Pair Production
abstract: The production of two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider has applications in Higgs-boson phenomenology and in new-physics searches. In fact, measurements would provide more insight if a percent-level theoretical prediction were available. We account for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order strong-interaction effects in the cross section for the first time. This is not only necessary to demonstrate the convergence of perturbation theory, but also results in a reduction of the theoretical uncertainty by a factor of 3 down to 3%. With this, we pave the way to improved analyses.

title: First Simultaneous Analysis of Transverse Momentum Dependent and Collinear Parton Distributions in the Proton
abstract: We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, W + charm, and jet production involving PDFs, as well as TMD Drell-Yan and Z -boson production data from fixed target and collider experiments sensitive to both TMD and collinear distributions. The analysis is performed at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for QCD resummation in TMD observables and next-to-leading order for observables described in collinear factorization. The combined analysis improves knowledge of both TMD and collinear PDFs, particularly in the sea-quark sector, providing a consistent simultaneous description of the aforementioned observables.

title: Wave-energy partition governs weak collisional damping in cold plasmas
abstract: Abstract Weak dissipation can control wave propagation, mode competition, andinstability thresholds in plasmas, yet the physical origin of largebranch-to-branch differences in collisional damping is often obscuredby dielectric-tensor calculations. We show that weak collisionaldamping in cold plasmas is governed by wave-energy partition. In theone-rate cold plasma model with independent-relaxation collisions, the damping rate of a positive-energycollisionless eigenmode equals, to leading order in weak collisions, the collision frequency multiplied by thefraction of the total wave energy stored in plasma motion. This resultrecasts the standard perturbative damping formula into a compact andphysically transparent law, immediately explaining why field-dominatedbranches such as whistlers can be much less damped than the collisionfrequency, whereas quasi-electrostatic modes can exhibit damping ofcomparable magnitude. Analytic examples for Langmuir, transverseelectromagnetic, whistler, and extraordinary waves show that theenergy-partition form classifies weak collisional damping acrossdistinct branches and provides a simple diagnostic for modecompetition in multibranch plasma-wave systems.

title: Realizing uniform implosion of double-cone ignition by combining a predictive model and Bayesian optimization
abstract: Abstract The direct-drive inertial confinement fusion (ICF) schemes like the double-cone ignition (DCI) scheme can efficiently utilize the laser energy, while it faces significant challenges in uniform implosion and achieving high areal density of the fuel. This is because of the P2 asymmetry driven by the laser and the high-mode Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI) growth. We propose an efficient optimization approach by integrating multiple algorithms and physical models to address these limitations. Based on two-dimensional (2D)radiation hydrodynamics simulations, a scaling law for the areal density is derived, incorporating laser parameters, target structure, and instability factors, all of which have significant effects on the areal density. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to optimize the irradiation positions and spot radius of the two-ring laser, improving the uniformity of laser intensity distribution on the target surface and thus reducing the P2 asymmetry. Combining one-dimensional (1D) simulations with the RTI growththeory, a quantitative predictive model for P2 asymmetry and a qualitative predictive model for high-mode RTI are established, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, the outputs of the predictive models are used as input parameters to perform Bayesian optimization for iteratively optimizing laser profile and target structure. The areal density of the DCI in 2D simulations increases from 0.156 g/cm² to 0.274 g/cm² with 2 ×16 kJ drive lasers. This method provides a new paradigm for the experimental design of DCI and polar direct-drive (PDD) scheme.

title: Impact of energetic alpha particles on core turbulence in an ARC-class fusion power plant
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the impact of fusion-born alpha particles on core turbulence and transport in the ARC tokamak fusion power plant [1] using linear and nonlinear gyrokinetic CGYRO [2] simulations. A significant reduction in ion-scale turbulent heat and particle fluxes is observed in the inner core (r/a ≤ 0.5), which is associated with multiscale interactions between fast ion-destabilized modes, zonal flows, and the background turbulence. A nonlinear upshift in the ITG critical gradient is observed in the simulations with fast alphas compared to those with artificially thermalized alphas. The turbulence reduction is found to scale benefi- cially with alpha particle density and plasma βe, and the radial extent of the turbulence suppression is limited to the volume containing a sig- nificant density of fast particles. The suitability of local gyrokinetics and potential impacts of fast ion effects on fusion performance are discussed.

title: Enhanced laser-driven directional neutron source via Bayesian optimization of cone targets
abstract: Abstract Laser-driven neutron sources, particularly beam-target neutron sources, hold significant potential for applications in neutron radiography, non-destructive inspection, nuclear astrophysics, etc. However, the quality of current beam-target neutron sources, especially neutron yield and divergence angle, still requires substantial improvement. Here, we present a novel laser-driven cone-target scheme to enhance the quality of neutron beams. Through integrated two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, it is demonstrated that the proposed scheme significantly enhances the ion acceleration by effectively focusing the laser pulse and guiding the electron beams. With the resulting increase in ion energy, a number of neutrons per laser shot of about 2.0×10 9 is achieved, which is 39 times higher than that from the plane target. Moreover, the scheme raises the forward-to-sideward yield ratio and makes the emission of the high-energy neutrons more forward-directed. Our theoretical model systematically elucidates the physical mechanisms governing high-energy ion generation, neutron yield enhancement and forward-emission optimization. Assisted by Bayesian Optimization, the influences of the target and laser parameters are also investigated and the optimal parameter ranges are identified, facilitating the experimental demonstration of laser-driven directional neutron sources.

title: Effect of NBI on thermal quench dynamics in TCV disruptions
abstract: Abstract A neutral beam injection (NBI) heat deposition model is implemented in the Disruption Runaway Electron Analysis Model (DREAM), accounting for the attenuation of the neutral beam particles, the resulting beam shine-through, and the partition of deposited energy between electrons and ions. The NBI model is applied to three TCV disruption discharges (#86634, #86645, and #86654) with different amounts of injected NBI power, and bayesian inference is used to constrain the heat transport and neon injection parameters. Sets of parameters are found which allow the simulations to reproduce the experimentally measured electron temperature, radiated power, and initial line-integrated density. The final runaway electron density is shown to be only weakly affected by NBI, and further comparisons between fluid and kinetic simulations indicate that a slight reduction in early runaway generation can be followed by enhanced runaway production at later times. Extrapolation to ITER also suggests that unrealistically large NBI powers would be required to produce a comparable effect. These results indicate that NBI can affect disruption dynamics in small and medium-size tokamaks, but is insufficient to affect the thermal quench dynamics in reactor-scale tokamaks.

title: Automated shape optimization of stellarator divertor targets via Chebyshev parameterization and differential evolution
abstract: Abstract Managing extreme heat fluxes in the form of strike lines on divertor target plates is a central challenge that hinders the progression of reactor-relevant stellarators. We present an automated, fast, non-gradient-based optimization framework for shaping open stellarator divertor targets, applied to the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) island divertor as a test case. The target surface geometry is parameterized using a Chebyshev spectral basis whose low-order modes naturally encode the physics motivated deformations, namely: translation, tilting and higher-order bending, which directly govern the incidence angle and flux tube connection-length distributions at the targetsurface. The heat flux distribution on a target surface is evaluated by EMC3 Lite, a fast three-dimensional Monte Carlo edge-plasma transport code that self-consistently solves an energy transport equation with a sheath boundary condition, thereby avoiding the fixed-velocity limitations of simpler field-line-diffusion proxies. A parallelized Differential Evolution algorithm explores the Chebyshev coefficient space, minimizing a composite objective that simultaneously reduces peak heat flux, promotes uniform heat spreading, and encourages power interception leaving the scrape-off layer. The optimizer redistributes the load toroidally rather than by broadening it across the field: the baseline plate collects 33% of its power in the final 0.84° of its toroidal span and almost nothing over φ ∈ [10, 20]°, whereas the optimized surface spreads the load over φ ∈ [0, 20]°, widening the toroidal deposition profile by a factor of 4.7.This results in a significant reduction of concentrated strike-line loading without sacrificing intercepted power. A secondary contribution is poloidal. At fixed toroidal angle the raised plate intercepts a broader radial swath of the island, widening the footprint by a further factor of 1.55-1.6. This is not flux expansion, which is measured to decrease by 16-32% between the two plate heights and therefore opposes the widening. Second-order Chebyshev modes are found to be essential because they reverse the sign of the curvature of Z(φ), letting the plate track the toroidal drift of the strike zone over the first half of its span and fall away from it over the second half, which is a combination that is inaccessible to pure tilting sured to decrease by 16-32% between the two plate heights and therefore opposes.

title: Isospin-symmetry violation – kaons and beyond
abstract: Abstract This report summarizes the presentations and discussions during the ISO-BREAK 25 Workshop “Isospin symmetry violation: kaons and beyond”, which was held at Jan Kochanowski University in Kielce on October 23–25, 2025. We address the current status of the isospin-symmetry breaking discovered by NA61/SHINE in nucleus–nucleus collisions at the CERN SPS, its confirmation by other experiments and studies in $${\textit{e}^+{+} \textit{e}^-}$$ e + + e - and deep inelastic scattering. In addition, we discuss the theoretical status as well as we outline experimental and theoretical priorities towards understanding this currently unexplained phenomenon.

title: Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Germanium by COHERENT
abstract: The COHERENT Collaboration reports the most precise measurement of the coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering cross section to date. This measurement was performed with COHERENT’s germanium detector array, Ge-Mini, at the Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. A cumulative exposure of 4.69 × 10 22 protons on target yielded a total number of observed counts of 124 − 12 + 14 and a flux-averaged cross section of 0.98 ± 0.10 ( statistical ) ± 0.10 ( systematic ) relative to the standard-model expectation of 5.9 × 10 − 39 cm 2 . The well-understood energy and timing distributions of the neutrino source allow for independent measurements of muon- and electron-neutrino scattering rates. This information is used to improve constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions mediated by heavy particles.

title: SOLPS-ITER simulation analysis on the synergistic effect of boron and neon in detached plasma on EAST
abstract: Abstract EAST experiments have demonstrated that combined neon (Ne) and boron (B) injection overcomes the narrow operational window of pure neon seeding, and compensates for the insufficient radiative capacity of B alone, establishing a stable ELM-suppressed H-mode with a partially detached outer divertor and good confinement (H₉₈ ~1) [Sun et al 2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 044002]. To reveal the underlying physical mechanisms, SOLPS-ITER simulations of Ne-B co-injection are performed under EAST conditions. Three mechanisms are identified. First, B and Ne form a poloidal radiation synergy: Ne radiates efficiently at Te ~20-27 eV near the X-point, while B fills the radiative gap below ~17 eV in the divertor region, together extending the energy dissipation zone from the X-point to the target and enabling deep energy detachment. Second, the B-enhanced D⁺-D charge exchange in the near-SOL amplifies momentum loss and substantially reduces the target particle flux. Third, the reduced Ne seeding rate through compensating B radiation is the dominant lever for lowering core radiation and Zeff, because core impurity content is governed by Ne, with its density exceeding that of B by nearly two orders of magnitude regardless of injection rate. Additionally, the deeper detachment state further promotes B deposition on the divertor target, reinforcing wall conditioning. These mechanisms provide a generalizable physics framework for mixed low-Z/high-Z impurity injection strategies on ITER and future fusion devices.

title: Incomplete fusion in 193 Ir( 12 C, x) 205 Bi reaction at E lab ≈ 5–7 AMeV
abstract: Abstract Low-energy heavy-ion induced reactions often involve incomplete fusion (ICF), but the dependence of ICF on various entrance-channel parameters remains unclear. In this work, we measure channel-by-channel production cross-sections of different evaporation residues populated via complete and/or ICF in 12 C+ 193 Ir system at E lab ≈ 64–84 MeV ( ≈ 5–7 AMeV) using the stacked-foil activation technique followed by offline γ -spectroscopy. Experimentally measured excitation functions (EFs) have been analyzed in the framework of the statistical model code PACE4 using different values of the level-density parameter ( a = A/9–A/13 MeV − 1 ). In the analysis of EFs, the x n and p x n channels (after correcting with their precursor contributions) have been explained fairly well with a = A/13 MeV − 1 ; however, almost all α -emitting channels showed substantial enhancement over PACE4 predictions, which has been interpreted as an inferred ICF contribution. The ICF fraction ( F ICF ) increases overall from 12% to 18% over the studied energy range (64–84 MeV). For better insights into the onset and strength of ICF, the variations of F ICF have been studied as a function of different entrance-channel parameters, which are found to increase with mass asymmetry, Coulomb factor, and neutron skin thickness. Further analysis suggests that the sharp-cut-off model, in which ICF is confined to ℓ > ℓ crit , does not fully hold for this system, with the ICF strength consistent with contributions from ℓ < ℓ crit . Projectile breakup-driven ICF is found to suppress complete fusion by ≈ 12 % and ≈ 6 % w.r.t. the universal fusion function and the improved fusion function, respectively. These findings highlight the critical role of projectile structure at 5–7 AMeV energies, with implications for high-spin spectroscopy and reaction modeling.

Soft H-L back transitions induced by RMP coils in high q 95 plasmas on EAST
abstract: Abstract Soft H-mode to L-mode (H-L) back transitions, combined with simultaneous particle and heat pumping via n = 2 resonant magnetic perturbations (RMPs), have been achieved in EAST plasmas at low safety factor ( q 95 = 3.5 − 4.0 ) without reducing auxiliary heating power (Shao et al 2024 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 66 035018). For the termination control of ITER, which is also equipped with RMP coils, this process inevitably drives the plasma toward a high q 95 , where the established n = 2 RMP is unlikely to produce a soft H-L back transition, because the edge-resonant surface at such high q 95 requires a high poloidal mode number m , and the n = 2 RMP field is strongly attenuated at such high m and couples only weakly to the edge. However, an n = 1 RMP can restore edge coupling, enabling reliable particle and heat pump-out without radiative collapse or current-profile magnetohydrodynamics risks on EAST. Within an operating window constrained by impurity and neutral beam injection conditions, both the n = 1 and n = 2 RMPs exhibit a reproducible energy confinement time threshold at the H-L transition τ e H-L ∼ 49 ms, which can serve as a control trigger.

title: Prospects for early heavy-quark measurements at the EIC
abstract: Abstract We assess the prospects for inclusive heavy-quark-pair electroproduction in electron–proton ( ep ) and electron–nucleus ( e A) collisions, alongside double-charm-pair ( $$D^0 \bar{D}^0$$ D 0 D ¯ 0 and $$D^0D^0$$ D 0 D 0 ) electroproduction in ep collisions, during the early operational phase of the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Based on the anticipated beam energies and luminosities of the EIC, we estimate the total cross sections and differential distributions for photon virtuality $$Q^2$$ Q 2 , heavy-quark transverse momentum, and rapidity. This analysis evaluates different Bjorken- x ( $$x_\textrm{Bj}$$ x Bj ) intervals across a range of $$Q^2$$ Q 2 values. Expected event yields are estimated from the projected integrated luminosities of the early science programme, demonstrating the substantial improvement in statistical precision over previous HERA measurements at moderate and large $$x_{\textrm{Bj}}$$ x Bj . For electron–nucleus collisions, we compute the nuclear modification ratio $$R^{e\text {A}}$$ R e A within collinear factorisation using nuclear parton distribution functions, and identify the kinematic regimes in which shadowing, anti-shadowing, and EMC-like suppression are accessible with early EIC data. These results are intended to serve as a parton-level baseline to support feasibility studies and to provide a reference for future higher-order theoretical and experimental investigations at the EIC.

title: Real-Time String Dynamics in a 2 + 1 D Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: String Breaking, Glueball Formation, Baryon Blockade, and Tension Reduction
abstract: Understanding flux string dynamics can provide insight into quark confinement and hadronization. First-principles quantum and numerical simulations have mostly focused on toy-model Abelian lattice gauge theories (LGTs). With the advent of state-of-the-art quantum simulation experiments, it is timely to study string dynamics in non-Abelian LGTs beyond one spatial dimension. Using tensor network methods, we simulate the real-time string dynamics of a 2 + 1 D SU(2) Yang-Mills LGT with dynamical matter. In the strong-coupling regime and at resonance, string breaking occurs via a sharp Casimir reduction, along with meson and baryon-antibaryon formation, a distinctively non-Abelian feature. At finite baryon density, we discover a mechanism that delays string breaking. Away from resonance, the magnetic term drives purely non-Abelian fluctuations: glueball-like excitations and self-crossed strings that resolve two SU(2) intertwiners with distinct dynamics. For higher-energy strings, we uncover representation-dependent tension-reduction resonances. Our findings serve as a guide for upcoming quantum simulators of non-Abelian LGTs.

title: Precision Hypernuclear Structure from Interaction Cross Sections
abstract: We establish interaction cross sections as a quantitative structural observable for hypernuclei. Using the hypertriton, H Λ 3 , as the most stringent benchmark, microscopic three-body wave functions are combined with a finite-range coupled-channel Glauber calculation and Bayesian inversion. For H Λ 3 + C 12 at 1.5 GeV / nucleon , the interaction cross section decreases from about 1150 to 750 mb as the Λ separation energy B Λ increases from 0.1 to 0.5 MeV, while propagated reaction-model uncertainties remain near 5%. A measurement therefore supplies a direct inversion σ I → r m → B Λ , constraining both the matter radius and the Λ separation energy. The framework provides the missing quantitative link between proposed interaction-cross-section measurements and the spatial structure of an already formed hypernucleus. Although demonstrated for the hypertriton, the methodology is readily extendable to other weakly bound hypernuclei.

title: Applications of a novel model-based real-time observer for electron density profile control experiments in TCV
abstract: Abstract Real-time estimation and control of the electron plasma density profile is fundamental for monitoring and regulating particle confinement, fusion power, heating efficiency, exhaust performance, impurity concentration, and proximity to the density limit (Greenwald et al Nucl. Fusion 28 2199–207) in present and future tokamaks. This work presents the experimental applications of a multi-rate electron density observer (Pastore Fusion Eng. Des. 192 113615) based on RAPDENS (Blanken Fusion Eng. Des. 126 87–103), integrated into the TCV plasma control system, to control the density profile in a range of plasma scenarios relevant to future fusion power plants. Three main experimental contributions are reported. First, the observer enables control of the line-averaged electron density within the last-closed flux surface ( NEL LCFS ) in ohmic, nitrogen-seeded plasmas with alternative divertor geometries, decoupling upstream density from scrape-off layer pickup in the interferometer signal—a limitation of the traditional control scheme. Second, local control of the central electron density below the ECH cutoff is demonstrated in L-mode plasmas with mixed ECH and neutral beam injection heating, where auxiliary-heating-induced profile peaking is treated as a disturbance to the control task. Real-time estimation and adjustment of the electron pinch velocity-to-diffusivity ratio ν / D improves the spatial accuracy of the profile reconstruction, especially in the core region. The underlying turbulent transport in this scenario is characterised via linear and non-linear gyrokinetic simulations with GENE, confirming quantitatively a TEM-dominated pumpout regime during ECH, which affects the amount of gas flux needed to sustain the target density reference. Last, simultaneous control of the edge-normalised density fraction and toroidal beta is demonstrated in high-performance H-mode plasmas ( β N ≈ 2.15 , f GW ≈ 0.80 ), yielding reproducible scenarios with a device-agnostic density metric and robust handling of interferometer fringe jumps.

title: Particle Correlations in Jets
abstract: We study particle correlations in high energy jets by comparing the measured energy-energy correlator with that constructed from two individual energy flows with respect to the jet axis. This comparison demonstrates that the genuine correlations are stronger at moderate or large angles across all jet energies, indicating that they are coming from correlated splitting. Meanwhile, at small angles, they increase with jet energy, exhibiting a peculiar pattern that can be used to explore jet energy loss in heavy-ion collisions. This method will provide a unique tool to disentangle different physics by comparing the genuine correlations in jet energy-energy correlators between heavy-ion collisions and proton-proton collisions.

title: O 16 ( p , γ ) F 17 Reaction and the C and O Isotopic Ratios in Red Giant Branch Stars
abstract: The O 16 : O 17 isotopic ratio is a widely used tracer of nucleosynthesis and mixing processes in red giant stars. Its value depends on the rates of the proton-capture reactions responsible for the production and destruction of O 16 and O 17 among which the O 16 ( p , γ ) F 17 reaction plays a central role, as it involves both isotopes. This work reports on a new measurement of the O 16 ( p , γ ) F 17 cross section carried out at the Laboratory for Underground Nuclear Astrophysics (LUNA) over a center-of-mass energy range of 200–380 keV, a region previously unexplored by experimental studies. Two complementary techniques were employed: prompt gamma-ray detection and activation. The results obtained with the two techniques are consistent within experimental uncertainties. From the measured cross sections and existing literature data, we evaluate a new thermonuclear reaction rate, which is then used to demonstrate how simultaneous measurements of stellar carbon and oxygen isotopic ratios constrain the initial mass and the extent of the mixing events in red giant branch stars. In particular, we demonstrate how the C 12 : C 13 abundance ratio is primarily sensitive to the temperature T max attained during mixing, whereas the O 16 : O 17 abundance ratio is highly sensitive to the initial stellar mass M i . Therefore, simultaneous measurements of these isotopic ratios can disentangle and place stringent constraints on M i and T max , and the remaining uncertainty is now dominated by stellar abundance measurements rather than nuclear-physics inputs.

title: Neutrino Emissivity in Δ -Direct-Urca Processes inside Neutron Stars
Two-body scattering observables from finite-volume real-time evolution
abstract: Abstract We study two-body scattering observables from real-time evolution in a finite periodic box. The system consists of two distinguishable particles on a two-dimensional lattice interacting through pointlike s - and p -wave interactions. We evolve their wave packets in real time, define detector observables through angular wedges in the relative coordinate, and attach infinite-volume labels obtained from the bound-state pole equation and the low-energy scattering amplitude. We train a convolutional neural network on this data and test its performance on previously unseen finite volume scattering data and find that is able to predict the total magnitude and angular shape of cross sections for previously unseen Hamiltonians.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Theoretical study of multinucleon transfer reactions with a 208 Pb target using master equation
abstract: Abstract Combining with the dinuclear system concept, we developed the traditional master equation approach by incorporating the nucleon transfer probability influenced by the optimal Q -value. That approach was applied to calculate the production cross sections of the fragments in the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb, 136 Xe+ 208 Pb, and 136 Xe+ 198 Pt reactions and the mass distributions in 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 136 Xe+ 208 Pb reactions. The calculated results are in favorable agreement with the available experimental data. For the observed asymmetry in the production cross sections of the fragments for 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 40 Ca+ 208 Pb systems, it is attributed to the constraint of the optimal Q -value window on the transfer process. Due to the small difference between Q -value of nucleon transfer and optimal Q -value, the projectile 58 Ni and 40 Ca tend to pickup neutrons and strip protons. Furthermore, owing to the shell effect, the Q -values for the 40 Ca+ 208 Pb reaction in the proton pickup and neutron stripping channels are farther from the optimal Q -value than those for the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb reaction, making it harder for 40 Ca to lose neutrons and gain protons than for 58 Ni.

title: Cross-shell excitations and the impact of the high- j intruder orbital in 94 Tc
abstract: Abstract The high-spin level structure of the N = 51 nucleus 94 Tc has been investigated using large-scale shell-model calculations with different effective interactions. Calculations including neutron excitations across the N = 50 shell gap reproduce the main features of the experimental level scheme and identify neutron core excitation as an important mechanism for generating high-spin states. An extended model space including the 1 h 11 / 2 neutron orbital provides improved agreement with experiment. Wave-function analyses show that 1 h 11 / 2 configurations dominate over a broad spin range, while N = 50 core excitations are largely suppressed. The results reveal the evolution of the competition between 1 h 11 / 2 excitation and N = 50 core breaking with increasing spin.

title: The multiscale nonlinear interactions between kinetic ballooning mode and drift wave turbulence critical for confinement improvement of hybrid fusion plasmas
abstract: Abstract Nonlinear suppression of short-wavelength drift wave turbulence by long-wavelength kinetic ballooning mode in tokamak fusion plasma is proposed to be the main cause for confinement improvement in the core of hybrid fusion plasmas. Specifically, the ambient ion temperature gradient(ITG) turbulence, which can contribute considerable transport flux if not mitigated, is fully suppressed in the presence of kinetic ballooning mode(KBM). KBM is demonstrated to be robustly unstable from fully electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. While its flux is low under low magnetic shear, KBM can generate significant stabilizing zonal flow whose velocity well surpasses the normalized linear growth rate of ITG. This multiscale physics phenomenon is convincingly verified on a representative ASDEX-Upgrade hybrid scenario plasma.

title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
abstract: Abstract Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Disruption halo currents and voltages measured on the HBT-EP tokamak
abstract: Abstract This paper presents measurements of disruption halo currents on the High Beta Tokamak—Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) experiment using 4 high-field side (HFS) tile arrays spaced at equal intervals of toroidal angle. Current flow through the tiles is measured using Rogowski coils external to the tokamak vessel. Tiles can also be operated as floating probes measuring their voltage with respect to the local chamber. Poloidal and toroidal distributions of halo currents are presented, along with a description and explanation of voltage measurements for both axisymmetric and rotating halo currents. Arcing on tiles generates current to components that greatly exceeds ion saturation current limits in the presence of an intact sheath. Furthermore, arcing is observed to occur more frequently as halo current magnitude increases. Measurements of voltages by operating tiles in floating configuration are found to be consistent with the halo voltage generation model presented in Boozer (2013 Phys. Plasmas 20 082510). The dependence of tile polarity on poloidal position as well as halo current peak shape are explained using tile voltage measurements.

title: Calculation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the D–T fusion process in tokamak reactors
abstract: Abstract In the deuterium tritium (D–T) fusion reaction an alpha particle is released with the kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . Since the fusion reaction is governed by the strong interaction, the alpha particle is almost instantaneously accelerated to the final state with its kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . According to the classical electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation should be emitted in such an acceleration process. In this work, we calculate the electromagnetic radiation in the D–T fusion process using both the classical electrodynamics and the quantum mechanical models. The radiation is compared with the radiation from the core plasma bremsstrahlung for pure D–T plasmas in large tokamaks. The ratio between the radiation from the D–T fusion reaction and bremsstrahlung depends only on the plasma temperature. The radiation from the D–T fusion reaction is stronger than that from bremsstrahlung if the frequency is higher than a critical value. Although the predicted radiation is much weaker than its high frequency counterpart, it is still possible to be detected in the high fusion gain reactors under some circumstances. Its effect should also be taken into account if one uses the gamma-ray emission spectrum to diagnostic for plasma profiles in tokamaks.

title: AI-based plasma equilibrium parameter inference in KSTAR for DEMO-relevant reactors using only ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a deep neural network for high-fidelity equilibrium parameter inference, serving as a surrogate of the magnetic EFIT reconstruction and relying exclusively on ex-vessel magnetic signals. The objective is to circumvent the long-term integrity constraints of in-vessel magnetic diagnostics in the nuclear environment of the Demonstration Fusion Power Reactor (DEMO)-relevant devices. Using KSTAR data (2021-2024), a baseline model trained solely on measured ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics (the Measurement-only model) is compared with an Augmented model, which addresses informational sparsity via virtual-sensor signals computed from the GEQDSK. The Augmented model achieves predictive fidelity comparable to off-line EFIT, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) above 0.99 and a range-normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE) of 0.332 % averaged over all parameters, against 2.385 % for the Measurement-only model. Because the virtual-sensor inputs derive from the EFIT solutions that define the targets, these figures quantify the surrogate fidelity with respect to the magnetic EFIT and constitute an upper bound on the accuracy attainable with physically installed ex-vessel probes, not that of an independent reconstruction. As the reference floor for the Measurement-only model, the magnetic fitting residuals of the parent EFIT reconstructions against the measured probe signals are quantified, yielding pooled range-normalized residuals of 1.55-3.87 % per campaign with structured, campaign-persistent components that random noise perturbations do not emulate. Robust accuracy is maintained during neutral beam injection (NBI)-induced transients, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution verifies that the Augmented model captures the underlying magnetohydrodynamic physics, specifically the Shafranov shift. With a median single-forward-pass inference latency of 3.47 ms and a 99th percentile of 3.53 ms, the framework is a viable surrogate for conventional numerical solvers. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that an idealized, EFIT-consistent realization of a densified ex-vessel sensor configuration retains sufficient information for high-precision equilibrium parameter inference, provided that magnetic probes are physically installed at the designated locations. This establishes the information-content prerequisite for ex-vessel-only inference in DEMO. The accuracy attainable from physically installed probes, subject to conductor-model, calibration and structured measurement-model errors, is not established and requires validation against measured ex-vessel signals.

title: A novel high-performance confinement regime in a tokamak driven by tearing mode locking and rotation shear
abstract: Abstract In magnetically confined fusion plasmas, tearing mode (TM) locking is conventionally regarded as detrimental, often halting rotation and triggering disruptions. Contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate that locked TMs can enhance confinement by inducing an internal transport barrier (ITB). Specifically, the interaction between a locked outer plasma region and neutral beam injection (NBI)-driven core rotation generates a broad and intense toroidal velocity shear layer, which suppresses turbulence and improves core confinement. Beam emission spectroscopy and charge exchange recombination spectroscopy confirm a substantial reduction in turbulent transport and a rise in core ion temperature exceeding T i > 9 keV . This phenomenon—termed the Locking-Induced Flow and Transport (LIFT) mode—transforms a traditionally disruptive mechanism into a confinement enhancement strategy.

title: Vector meson photoproduction on the nucleus and the extraction of the nuclear suppression factor using asymmetric beams
abstract: Abstract The cross-section for photoproduction of a vector meson on a nucleus is usually determined in nucleus-nucleus collisions, which introduces a twofold ambiguity as to which nucleus emitted the photon. This can be resolved in asymmetric collisions of protons and nuclei, where the ratio of photoproduction cross-sections on the proton and nucleus directly measures the nuclear suppression factor with minimal model dependence. The feasibilty of using existing and future proton-lead collisions at the LHC is evaluated.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Global gyrokinetic simulations of electromagnetic turbulence in STEP
abstract: Abstract This paper presents gradient-driven global electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations for a conceptual burning flat-top operating point of STEP (Tholerus et al 2024 Nucl. Fusion 64 106030), STEP-EC-HD, and investigates how non-local effects influence the nonlinear saturation and transport of the electromagnetic turbulence at finite β . Local gyrokinetic simulations have shown that including δ B ∥ is essential for the dominant hybrid kinetic ballooning modes, or hKBMs, to be unstable in STEP (Kennedy et al 2024 Nucl. Fusion 64 086049). Using the long-wavelength δ B ∥ solver (Sheffield et al 2024 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 67 015028) implemented in GENE (Jenko et al 2000 Phys. Plasmas 7 1904–10), this work demonstrates that the linear mode spectrum can be accurately captured in global geometry, which results in good agreement with an ensemble of local flux-tube simulations. The global framework reproduces the hKBMs identified in Kennedy et al (2023 Nucl. Fusion 63 126061), while microtearing modes remain challenging to resolve due to their shorter radial scales. Nonlinear simulations reveal clear evidence of an electromagnetic transition to states with extremely large heat fluxes, consistent with local simulations and with the predicted loss of zonal-flow regulation for this proposed operating point (Kennedy et al 2026 Nucl. Fusion ). These findings establish the capability of global gyrokinetics to capture finite- β dynamics in STEP-like plasmas and motivate future work to identify the conditions governing this transition.

title: Pion emission source shape in UrQMD Au + Au collisions at STAR energies
abstract: Abstract Femtoscopic measurements of two-pion Bose–Einstein correlations have established that particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions are well described by Lévy $$\alpha $$ α -stable distributions, motivating systematic studies across a wide range of collision energies. In this work, we present a three-dimensional femtoscopic analysis of pion pairs in Au + Au collisions simulated with the UrQMD model for collision energies $$\sqrt{s_{NN}}=3$$ s NN = 3 – $$27\,\textrm{GeV}$$ 27 GeV , taking the RHIC BES-II range of collider and fixed target experiment energies for reference. Using Lévy-type source parameterisations, we extract the Lévy index $$\alpha $$ α , the three-dimensional radii $$R_\textrm{out}$$ R out , $$R_\textrm{side}$$ R side , $$R_\textrm{long}$$ R long , and the pair multiplicity parameter $$\lambda ^{*}$$ λ ∗ (related to the correlation strength $$\lambda $$ λ ). We investigate their dependence on the transverse mass ( $$m_T$$ m T ) and collision energy, along with derived quantities such as the radius difference $$R_{\textrm{diff}}^2=R_{\textrm{out}}^2-R_\textrm{side}^2$$ R diff 2 = R out 2 - R side 2 and the ratio $$R_\textrm{out}/R_\textrm{side}$$ R out / R side . We find that $$R_\textrm{out,side,long}$$ R out,side,long all decrease with increasing $$m_T$$ m T and increase with collision energy, consistent with collective expansion, $$R_\textrm{long}$$ R long showing the strongest and $$R_\textrm{side}$$ R side the weakest energy dependence. The Lévy index $$\alpha $$ α decreases with collision energy, with a larger $$m_T$$ m T -dependence towards higher energies. The $$\lambda ^{*}$$ λ ∗ parameter is consistent with a constant close to unity in the absence of pions from long-lived resonances. These results provide a baseline for future comparisons with experimental measurements from the STAR Collaboration, contributing to constraints on the QCD phase diagram.

title: System identification simulations using the Advanced Fluid Neutral model and Wide Grid formalism in SOLPS-ITER.
abstract: Abstract This work presents a first step towards using the SOLPS-ITER code package for synthetic system identification using multisine perturbations. Numerical modelling is used to replicate system identification experiments performed to establish exhaust control done on MAST-U. These experiments involve perturbing the gas injection rate and observing the SOL response in the frequency domain. The model used is the Advanced Fluid Neutral (AFN) model of SOLPS-ITER, implemented in the Wide Grids (WG) version of the code. The grid was generated with the Grid Optimization and Adaptation Toolbox (GOAT) and extends to the vessel wall, to enable calculating fluid neutral parameters across the entire domain. New boundary condition types were implemented in the code to allow for multisine gas injection perturbations, as well as reservoir models for remote vessel regions without plasma. In steady state, it is possible to simulate plasmas ranging from attached to deeply detached using different gas injection rates. This allows for comparison between simulation and experimental results at similar levels of detachment. Comparison between simulation and experimental data in the frequency domain shows that the AFN SOLPS-ITER simulations predict faster response times to divertor fuelling perturbations than the experiments, likely in part due to the fluid approximation used for the neutrals. When including the reservoir models for remote vessel regions the phase shifts increase, but are still too low compared to experiments.

title: Uncovering hidden systematics in neural network models for high energy physics
abstract: Abstract Neural networks (NNs) are inherently multidimensional classifiers that learn complex, non-linear relationships among input observables. While their flexibility enables unprecedented performance in high-energy physics (HEP) analyses, it also makes them sensitive to small variations in their inputs. Consequently, the propagation and estimation of systematic uncertainties in NN-based models remain an open challenge. There are indications that uncertainties derived in control regions or from nominal variations of input features can underestimate the sensitivity of a trained model, potentially leaving relevant directions in feature space untested. Inspired by adversarial-attack studies in machine learning, we explore how subtle perturbations, bounded by feature-wise experimental resolution scales, can lead to changes in NN outputs while keeping one-dimensional distributions and linear correlations nearly unchanged. Using representative HEP tasks spanning event classification and object identification, we demonstrate that networks can be systematically ‘fooled’ within these prescribed envelopes. We introduce this construction as a stress test of hidden model sensitivity. The resulting performance shift is a worst-case envelope within the assumed, idealized uncertainty model; it is not by itself a calibrated experimental systematic uncertainty or evidence for a bias in nature.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Direct nuclear reaction as a tool for nuclear structure and astrophysics
abstract: Abstract The study of nuclear structure has evolved significantly with the exploration of nuclei far from stability, revealing phenomena such as the modification of shell closures, the emergence of halos, and clustering. This review examines direct nuclear reactions as a primary experimental tool for probing these exotic structures and constraining astrophysical reaction rates, with an emphasis on the experimental observables that connect exotic nuclear structure, indirect astrophysical constraints, and modern inverse-kinematics instrumentation. We discuss the theoretical frameworks and experimental applications of elastic and inelastic scattering, transfer reactions, and knockout reactions. Special attention is given to the role of these mechanisms in mapping shell evolution and in characterizing nuclear deformation and α -clustering. Furthermore, the review highlights the intersection of nuclear structure and astrophysics, detailing indirect approaches such as the asymptotic normalization coefficient technique and the Trojan horse method for determining key stellar reaction rates at low energies. Finally, state-of-the-art instrumentation is surveyed, including high-resolution spectrometers, active target time projection chambers, and storage rings, which enable high-precision measurements in inverse kinematics.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Skyrme-quark–meson-coupling energy density functional predictions to nuclear ground state properties
abstract: Abstract We present a systematic study of nuclear ground-state properties obtained with the Skyrme quark–meson coupling (SQMC) energy density functional and compare them with results from the SLy4d Skyrme parameterisation. The SQMC functional is constructed using the quark–meson coupling (QMC) model, which incorporates the internal quark structure of the nucleon and results in a significant reduction in the number of free parameters. We investigate binding energies, two-nucleon separation energies, charge radii, and quadrupole deformations across a broad range of nuclei. Particular attention is devoted to the isovector dependence of the spin–orbit interaction derived within the QMC model, and its impact on the binding energies of neutron-rich nuclei relevant to the r-process. We find that the SQMC functional provides a reasonable description of nuclear ground-state properties in comparison with SLy4d.
